passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text: Fresh to your training, your first task is simple: Speak to Master Shang Xi.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Sandy Fist
passages.text:
I'd like to observe you putting your new weapon to use, my young student. This will aid me in determining what degree of training will be best suited to your talents.

We have many training targets in the training grounds below. Practice your attacks upon them, and return to me once you're feeling comfortable with your new weapon.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Sandy Fist
passages.text: The training targets are just down the hill. Come back to me once you're finished.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Sandy Fist
passages.text:
Not bad, <name>. You may indeed have chosen the proper path.

Good. Let us continue.

passages.title: The First Sign of Winter
passages.text: At the stream below rests a single lotus flower. Within this lotus lies a sign of things to come. Bring it to me that I might show you.

passages.title: The Disciple's Challenge
passages.text:
<name>, I see great strength and great courage in you, and an unsurpassed purity of soul.

The hour is young, but I think you may be ready to face a greater challenge.

Go to the bottom of the stairs, and cross the bridge. There, you will find Jaomin Ro, one of our eldest students. Challenge and defeat him in honorable combat, and this first phase of your training will be complete.

passages.title: The Disciple's Challenge
passages.text: You truly impress, <name>. It seems certain that the path of the <class> is indeed the path for you.

passages.title: Aysa of the Tushui
passages.text:
In such a short time, you've shown me that you have the potential to be a great <class>. The training grounds are behind you, but now you must prove yourself by facing a far greater challenge, one that none of my students have accomplished.

I want you to return Huo, the spirit of fire, to the Temple of Five Dawns.

My two other most gifted students will help you in this task. The first is Aysa Cloudsinger. Seek her out at the pool to the west.

passages.title: Aysa of the Tushui
passages.text:
You came for Aysa? You... you really shouldn't interrupt her until she finishes her exercises. She doesn't speak to anyone until her routine is done.

In the meantime, could you maybe help me? I had some bad luck with forest sprites.

passages.title: The Way of the Tushui
passages.text:
It's a pleasure to meet you, <class>. I am Aysa, of the Tushui.

I've spent much time in thought since Master Shang told me we would be searching for Huo, the spirit of fire. I know where he resides, but not how to reach him. The answers are close, however.

Come with me to the Cave of Meditation nearby. It is a place of great wisdom. I will meditate there, open my mind, and the path shall find us.

passages.title: The Way of the Tushui
passages.text:
Your path is set before you. You will be the one to rekindle the spirit of fire and bring it to the safety of the temple.

This will not be the only time you and Aysa work together. She is strong and wise. You can trust in her.

passages.title: The Way of the Huojin
passages.text:
We call those vicious monkeys swinging into town hozen. They keep to themselves normally, but they know something bad is coming, so they're here to steal our supplies.

In situations like this, the clear answer is the only answer. These monkeys will leave when we force them to leave! To not defend our town and those we love would be the only true crime. Thus is the way of the Huojin.

passages.title: The Way of the Huojin
passages.text: You've got some fight in you! I think I like you!

passages.title: Kindling the Fire
passages.text:
Now that that's done with, let's get to it then!

Huo, the spirit of fire, hungers for dry dogwood root kindling. It grows among the trees south of the village. It should be easy enough for you to gather some.

passages.title: Kindling the Fire
passages.text: I hope you're not shy about getting your hands dirty.

passages.title: Kindling the Fire
passages.text: <name>! You've returned, roots in hand! You're a down-to-business kind of guy, aren't you? I like that!

passages.title: The Missing Driver
passages.text:
My driver went running off after the sprites just after they attacked. I don't think they'll really do him any harm, but I need him back to help me clean up the mess by the cart.

He chased them off towards the cliffs to the north. If you head that direction, you should find him quickly.

passages.title: The Missing Driver
passages.text: You are too kind, <class>.

passages.title: The Spirit's Guardian
passages.text:
You've done very well this far, my student. You have the materials you need to rekindle Huo, the spirit of fire.

In the cave to the southwest he awaits, but he is guarded by Master Li Fei, the pandaren elder you met in the Cave of Meditation. Go to Master Li Fei with the offerings. Prove yourself, then meet with Huo.

passages.title: The Spirit's Guardian
passages.text: Life isn't about finding yourself. Life is about creating yourself. There is a path before you, but you choose the trials you will face, and the trials you will overcome.

passages.title: Only the Worthy Shall Pass
passages.text: It is time for you to face me. With these three fires illuminating your potential, we will see with certainty whether your resolved soul is truly worthy of passing.

passages.title: Only the Worthy Shall Pass
passages.text: Remember always, the superior warrior is modest in his speech, but exceeds in his actions.

passages.title: Huo, the Spirit of Fire
passages.text:
You are worthy of passing, <class>.

Huo, the spirit of fire rests in the chamber beyond. Let him feast upon the kindling you've gathered, and use the wind to fan his flames. Doing so should endear you to him. Once he is ignited, if he is willing, lead him to the Temple of Five Dawns, the building standing high in the center of the island.

passages.title: Huo, the Spirit of Fire
passages.text: <Huo rests quietly within the pool.>

passages.title: Huo, the Spirit of Fire
passages.text: <Through the glare, it looks like Huo is smiling. He seems to have warmed up to you.>

passages.title: The Passion of Shen-zin Su
passages.text:
<Huo bounces around excitedly, ready to follow you.>

<Master Shang Xi told you to bring Huo to meet him at the Temple of Five Dawns in the center of the island. Your next destination lies before you.>

passages.title: The Passion of Shen-zin Su
passages.text:
<name>, you've done very well. Huo, the spirit of fire, is here. The temple flames are reignited. You accomplished the challenge I put before you, and with seeming ease.

There is a greater purpose in bringing Huo to the temple. It is time that I tell you more of things to come.

passages.title: Items of Utmost Importance
passages.text:
Amberleaf scamps swarmed my cart and stole most of the training supplies I was bringing up to the training grounds. They've always been troublemakers, but they've never been this aggressive before. I don't know what happened.

Please, help me recover my supplies.

passages.title: Items of Utmost Importance
passages.text: You needn't worry about hurting the sprites. They're really just living plants when it comes down to it - they'll resprout later.

passages.title: Items of Utmost Importance
passages.text: Thank you! You're an honorable <class>. They've taught you well.

passages.title: The Singing Pools
passages.text:
It is crucial that we bring all of the three remaining spirits back safely. I am too old to do this myself, and for all their strengths, both Aysa and Ji are single-minded in their ideals.

You possess all the qualities of a hero, and a balance that they do not. It is you that must do this.

Shu, the spirit of water is somewhere in the singing pools to the east. Find Aysa there and work with her to locate him. We are all depending on you.

passages.title: The Singing Pools
passages.text:
It's good to see you again, <name>.

This is the pool of the skunk, as I'm sure you noticed.

Over the many ages of Shen-zin Su, animals have died in some of these magical pools. Through their deaths, their spirits were infused into the waters, and anyone touching those waters will take their form.

There are several cursed pools here, some more dangerous than others.

passages.title: Ji of the Huojin
passages.text:
Another of my most talented students is awaiting you in Wu-Song Village to the northwest. He is of a different mind than Aysa, but in their differences, they bring balance to each other.

Ji Firepaw will instruct you on gathering the offerings for the spirit of fire. Trust in his wisdom.

passages.title: Ji of the Huojin
passages.text:
Hello! You look poised and confident... I like that!

I've heard some rather impressive whispers about you from the training grounds. If you're half as capable as they say, I think you and I are going to be good friends!

passages.title: Fanning the Flames
passages.text:
Strange thing about wind, it can be hard to wrap your hands around it.

Best practice for me has been finding some sort of living wind. If it can punch you, you can punch it back, and it won't slip through your grasp.

Head over to the Shrine of the Summer Breeze to the south and summon just such a living wind using this wind stone. Best it, gather a Fluttering Breeze from it, and come back over this way so that we can figure out what's next.

passages.title: Fanning the Flames
passages.text: When opportunity rises, it is our responsibility to reach out and grab it. Second guessing is as good as giving up.

passages.title: Fanning the Flames
passages.text: You know what it is to seize opportunity. I think you and I are kindred spirits, <name>.

passages.title: The Lesson of Stifled Pride
passages.text:
Facing a living opponent is a very different thing from the stationary targets in the yard. Living opponents strike back. There is the very real fear of failure, and sometimes, even death.

You must have the courage to overcome those fears.

Challenge the other trainees within the temple or down the steps below, and defeat them.

passages.title: The Lesson of Stifled Pride
passages.text: There is a time for meditation and contemplation, and there is a time for action. Diving the balance between the two is one of the greatest wisdoms we seek.

passages.title: The Lesson of Stifled Pride
passages.text:
Intriguing, my young pupil.

Most of the other trainees have been here for quite some time, but you are able to match them even within this first hour.

This speaks well of you, but there are yet other lessons I would see you learn.

passages.title: Kill Stuff
passages.text: I really need you to kill some stuff for me. It's pretty important.

passages.title: Collect Things
passages.text: The Quest Wizard demands Stuff Tails! Go now and fetch them.

passages.title: Take Care of It
Tipping the Scales
passages.text:
These blasted native monkey savages have been assaulting us since the day we put to shore!

We were holding our own until they kidnapped half our men, including the Admiral.

Just look at their numbers! They're endless, and we're standing on our last legs.

If you're here to get us out of this mess, go help take down some monkeys.

It's them or us, <race>!

passages.title: The King's Command
passages.text:
Greetings, <class>.

I have been asked to assemble a team for a high priority mission.

Please come to Stormwind Keep immediately for a briefing with King Varian Wrynn. I will be waiting in the King's war room.

passages.title: The King's Command
passages.text: Our role is of utmost importance. Admiral Taylor and his flagship have gone missing. More importantly, the young Prince was with him, and it is our primary objective to bring him back home safely.

passages.title: The Mission
passages.text:
Well, you heard the King. Admiral Taylor's last transmission came from somewhere in the southern seas.

We will begin our search from the air! Locating the Prince - the White Pawn - is of critical priority.

The Skyfire is fueled, supplied, and ready to depart. She and her crew idle in the sky just north of the harbor.

Make your last preparations, then meet Admiral Rogers on the deck. We will depart without delay.

passages.title: The Mission
passages.text: Ah, a veteran of the Cataclysm campaigns! Good, I could use more experienced hands.

passages.title: The Mission
passages.text:
That's a whole Horde base down there! Where was our intel?

Well <class>, it's time to see what this upgraded gunship is capable of.

passages.title: Flightmaster Down
passages.text:
I've taken stock of the missing, and among them is Donovar Murall, our Flightmaster.

He is not only a vital part of our crew, he is a dear friend as well.

Please find him and bring him back alive.

passages.title: Saving Snowpuff
passages.text:
<Donovar bursts into tears upon seeing you.>

Th-th-those blasted monkey hooligans d-d-dragged me inta these woods. I thot I were dunnert, but mah faithful Snowpuff came flyin' to mah rescue!

She fought 'em off and then they all jumped 'er! Wot with them apes prowlin' around, she's...

<Donovar blows his nose loudly.>

...she's done for! Wahaahaaaaaa! Unless...

Listen <class>, I saw Gingerleaf growing all over these woods. I beg ya, bring me some o' that healing herb and Snowpuff just might make et!

passages.title: Grove Stalkers
passages.text:
We're still trying to take stock of our crew after the fighting.

I'm afraid many of them are stranded out in the woods, probably wounded and fighting to survive.

We know that the forest to the north is full of vicious tigers.

Go clear them out of the woods. You'll give more of our men and women a chance to make it back alive.

passages.title: The Missing Admiral
passages.text:
Alright. According to the clues you found, that was Anduin's ship, and Admiral Taylor was the captain. 

And Admiral Taylor's last entry says he was going to fight off the hozen and protect the vessel after the shipwreck.

The locals say these hozen sometimes take prisoners, and I didn't see Taylor's corpse anywhere among the wreckage. So you'll probably find Taylor at the hozen encampment to the northeast.

Get going, we have no time to lose!

passages.title: The Missing Admiral
passages.text: <You found him, but the Admiral is unconscious. He looks on the verge of death.>

passages.title: Sunken Junk
passages.text:
Hey <name>!

The coast here is littered with scraps of tools and metal from the shipwreck.

The ordinary person might think that this is junk, but I'm sure I can salvage most of it. I once repaired a submarine using only a bronze tube and a luffa!

Get me some of the waterlogged scraps along the shore by the ship. I need them for my next project.

passages.title: Hozen Aren't Your Friends, Hozen Are Your Enemies
passages.text:
We've located an Alliance wreck to the south. Unfortunately, the locals have informed us that it's currently being scavenged by a group of creatures called "hozen."

By pillaging our wrecked ships, these creatures have already shown that they aren't friendly. We can't have them taking spoils from our ships, stealing our supplies, and worse, potentially capturing or killing any survivors.

Get down there and take them out! When you're done, meet up with Nodd Codejack, our SI:7 agent in the area.

passages.title: Hozen Aren't Your Friends, Hozen Are Your Enemies
passages.text:
Good work. Dirty creatures trying to kick us when we're down... 

That'll teach 'em to try and salvage an Alliance vessel!

passages.title: The Mission Continues
passages.text:
The King's flagship went aground not far from here.

Apparently, the ship signaled Anduin's safe arrival shortly after landing, but when they sent men to retrieve the Prince, he was gone.

I want to investigate the wreckage for clues.

Nodd and Sully are already at the crash site. Go east along the beach and see if they need help.

passages.title: The Path of War
passages.text:
I see you want to save your friend. I can help you, if you will help me.

First of all, it should be obvious that the fewer the Slingtail roaming around, the easier it will be to escape.

Kill the hozen guards around us, and we will be one step closer to freedom.

passages.title: The Path of War
passages.text: You fight well, foreigner.

passages.title: The Path of War
passages.text:
Ahahaha! You are brave.

An admirable trait.

passages.title: Freeing Our Brothers
passages.text:
You may be an outsider, but you and I have a common enemy in the hozen.

Many members of my tribe are trapped in cages nearby. I have also seen your... Alliance... soldiers as well.

I cannot leave without freeing my brethren, just as you cannot leave yours.

The Slingtail hold the keys to those cages. Find the keys and free our friends.

passages.title: Freeing Our Brothers
passages.text: Are they freed?

passages.title: Freeing Our Brothers
passages.text:
You have freed my brothers? Good.

We are in your debt.

passages.title: Ancient Power
passages.text:
Hozen skulls are prized tokens among my village.

We use them to perform ceremonial rites, and the older the skull, the more potent its magic.

Luckily for us, the hozen are careless, filthy beasts. They leave the skulls of their dead scattered among their huts and campfires.

Collect these skulls for me, and I will reward you handsomely.

passages.title: Ancient Power
passages.text: The skulls are precious to my tribe. How many have you collected?

passages.title: Ancient Power
passages.text:
It is good to see that you are so resourceful, <name>. It is a trait admired by my people.

The fine specimens you have brought me will produce powerful magic.

passages.title: Against the Odds
passages.text:
You and I are the only mission operatives who made it to base camp, <class>.

I saw the other SI:7 eject over the forest to the north.

You'd better go quickly and rescue any survivors.

passages.title: Jailbreak
passages.text:
Without healing, your friend Taylor will die. My village is just east of here, in the middle of the large lake.

I will take Taylor myself, but the fighting is most dangerous in that direction.

I need you to help clear a path through the hozen, so that I may run safely into my village.

Can you do this?

passages.title: Jailbreak
passages.text: Our conflict with the hozen goes back many generations.

passages.title: Jailbreak
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. Because of you, we were able to make it here safely.

passages.title: An Air of Worry
passages.text:
My sight has long since faded, but when the wind is right I can still smell the blossoms of Nectarbreeze Orchard as if they were in my own palm.

Today, though, their fragrance is muddled with smoke. Please, if you are able, check in on the orchard and see that things are okay. Perhaps my old nose is playing tricks on me.

You'll find the orchard to the southwest, beyond the statue of the Jade Serpent.

passages.title: An Air of Worry
passages.text: If you've come to speak with my fists, take your place in line. Otherwise, I could use your help.

passages.title: The Golden Dream
passages.text:
Ashyo must have experienced what we call the golden dream.

Many of us working here have seen it, too - often after a long day of toiling in the pools. It is said this vision--and the feeling of elation it brings--is a reward to the mind for working the body.

There IS an easier way, though we rarely resort to it anymore: a tea can be brewed using lotus root and dreamleaf, which grows around the shrine on the upper tier.

Bring the dreamleaf to Yan back in town and he can brew the tea for you.

passages.title: The Golden Dream
passages.text: Yes, did you need something?

passages.title: The Golden Dream
passages.text:
Ah... dreamleaf! So you want to see the Golden Dream, do you?

Come to think of it, I haven't seen the Dream in years - not since I was a cub spending long hours playing in the pools. Long before I took up the culinary arts.

Looks like you brought enough dreamleaf for two cups of tea... so why not?

Here's to better days!

passages.title: Kill Mogu Firestarters
passages.text:
As if the attack weren't bad enough, the mogu are setting these ancient orchards ablaze.

I cannot understand what they hope to achieve, but we must stop them. Clear out the orchard so these people have a livelihood to return to.

passages.title: Unbound
passages.text:
Can you see them, adventurer? Farmers from the orchard, tied up and under inspection. Being hauled off in chains.

The mogu value strength above all else. Anyone deemed fit for work will be sent to toil under their cruel whips.

As for the others, well...

Let's not waste any more time.

passages.title: Unbound
passages.text: Those ropes should give with a strong tug.

passages.title: Unbound
passages.text: The pandaren were subjected to mogu rule in ancient times - we'll never let it happen again.

passages.title: The Art of War
passages.text:
Lok'tar ogar, <race>. I am Nazgrim.

You are hereby ordered to present yourself at Grommash Hold immediately.

All in service to the Horde are to swear an oath of allegiance to their new Warchief.

Do not keep him waiting, <race>.

passages.title: The Art of War
passages.text: Blood and thunder, orc.

passages.title: The Art of War
passages.text: Ahh, good. You're here. And not a moment too soon...

passages.title: The Art of War
passages.text:
Lok'tar Ogar, old friend. It has been too long since last we spoke.

It is good to see that you emerged safely from the depths of Vashj'ir.

I am stationed here in Grommash Hold.

All in service to the Horde are to swear allegiance to their new Warchief.

You would do well not to keep him waiting, <name>.

passages.title: The Art of War
passages.text: Ahh, good. You're here. And not a moment too soon...

passages.title: Tian Monastery
passages.text:
People come from all over Pandaria to train at the Tian Monastery, just to the north of here. Probably because they never turn anybody down. They'll accept jinyu, hozen... or even a foreign <race> like you!

My childhood friend, Lin, just joined the monastery's order a few weeks ago. If you're interested in learning how our monks train, maybe you should go talk with her!

passages.title: Tian Monastery
passages.text: You've arrived at an exciting time. High Elder Cloudfall has agreed to take on a new class of trainees within the monastery. This could be my big chance to finally learn how to fight!

passages.title: The High Elder
passages.text:
How strange, to have such a foreign-looking <class> visiting our temple. Are you here to study?

You... you look very strong. You wouldn't have any trouble getting accepted into the monastery. You should talk to the High Elder, up on the balcony above.

passages.title: The High Elder
passages.text:
Welcome to Tian Monastery. I see young Lin has helped you understand the role we fill here in our hilltop village.

We are unaccustomed to outsiders. You would do us a great honor to train alongside our younglings. We do not have anything to offer you, <class>... except knowledge, and perhaps an appreciation of what it means to be pandaren.

passages.title: UNUSED
passages.text:
I have but one task for you, and it is a simple one. I would like you to speak with the spirits of the high elders that came before Cloudfall.

Their spirits have left their bodies, but they have not left this place. Go, speak with them, absorb their wisdom, and curry their favor.

I anxiously await your return.

passages.title: Your Training Starts Now
passages.text:
<Xiao does not look up from his bowl.>

Hey, new <guy/lady>! Glad to see you survived the banquet! Trial One: Complete!

<Xiao eats noisily.>

You'd better speak up with Instructor Xann. He'll be expecting you for your daily exercises.

<He continues eating. You suspect that he is done talking to you.>

passages.title: Your Training Starts Now
passages.text:
First, you drink too much beer... and then you show up to class late? Looks like you've already conformed to pandaren culture.

Let's begin.

passages.title: UNUSED
Groundskeeper Wu
passages.text:
We don't have many rules here, but we do have one particular rule that is worth remembering. If you want to eat...

<Xiao's stomach grumbles audibly.>

...you have to work. Groundskeeper Wu can give you your chores for the day. He's in the market, to the west.

passages.title: Groundskeeper Wu
passages.text:
<Wu addresses you sharply.>

<name>, is it? The High Elder's favored son? Yes, I remember you from the banquet.

Don't expect any special treatment from me, boy. You'll be working just as hard as the greenest pandaren trainee here.

Perhaps harder.

passages.title: Burning Bright
passages.text:
Might I ask a favor of you, trainee <name>?

Before I came to the monastery, I was a stranger to battle. During my time as a trainee, I performed adequately, but I was never placed in any real danger. Now, as a graduate and a wage-earning guard, I am expected to protect this perimeter at all costs.

I can handle greenwood sprites, but the tigers in the western Waxwood are something different altogether. Would you mind taking care of them for me?

passages.title: Burning Bright
passages.text: Please, do not speak of our arrangement with others. My cowardice shames me.

passages.title: Burning Bright
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. A thousand times, thank you.

passages.title: Zhi-Zhi, the Dextrous
passages.text:
Upon the hills to my right, you will find a hozen named Zhi-Zhi. He, too, won enough sparring matches to move up the ranks. I think he will provide you with more of a challenge.

Challenge him, and try to defeat him.

passages.title: Zhi-Zhi, the Dextrous
passages.text: Zhi-Zhi's style is different than that of most pandaren monks. He and his kind tend to have more... energy... than us.

passages.title: Zhi-Zhi, the Dextrous
passages.text: It appears that I must move you up the ranks yet again, <class>.

passages.title: Husshun, the Wizened
passages.text:
The jinyu are long-standing allies of the pandaren, and we welcome any of their kind into our monastery. Husshun, one of their elder shaman, is one of our newest trainees.

His skills as a monk are mediocre at best, but he is still a fierce combatant. He should provide you with the challenge that you deserve.

passages.title: Husshun, the Wizened
passages.text: I do not know why he decided to take the monastic path so late in life. It is not my place to ask. Such questions fall under the responsibility of our Spirit-Sage.

passages.title: Husshun, the Wizened
passages.text:
I must warn you, <class>:

If you continue defeating my best trainees, I will no longer be able to train you. And then you will have no excuse to enjoy the presence of my company.

Think wisely before you quickly dispatch any more of my students.

passages.title: A Test of Endurance
passages.text:
I have taught you everything that I can, <name>. It is time you spoke with Instructor Myang.

The fights that she stages are less traditional than the sparring matches I am used to. Nevertheless, the path of a traveling adventurer like yourself is unpredictable, and a broad knowledge of fighting styles is an admirable trait.

Farewell, <name>, and best of luck on the remainder of your training.

passages.title: A Test of Endurance
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>. You are becoming quite famous among the trainees here. I have already heard your name whispered several times, usually between the puffy and discolored lips one of your sparring partners.

I'm looking forward to working with you.

passages.title: UNUSED
passages.text:
Your training is over, young one. The cycle is complete. Thankfully, this particular cycle ends exactly where it started... with a banquet.

I will meet you over at the banquet grounds. I will likely be dancing on a table.

passages.title: The Lesson of Dry Fur
passages.text:
Through meditation, I intend to find a route to locating Shu. In the meantime, you would benefit from practice and discipline.

Your first task is the task of all trainees entering the pools: cross the balance poles to the west and ring the bell without falling into the pool.

Should you fall, the pool's curse will make it difficult to get on a pole again, so you will need to return to the edge of the pool to start over.

Oh, and beware the cranes.

passages.title: The Lesson of Dry Fur
passages.text: Good. You're a quick study.

passages.title: Stronger Than Reeds
passages.text:
Gather me reeds from the nearby pools.

Do not question why. Do, and then observe the results.

passages.title: Stronger Than Reeds
passages.text: Telling you of my strength means nothing. I must show you.

passages.title: Stronger Than Reeds
passages.text:
Good.

No number of reeds have ever withstood my might.

Step back, and let me dispel your doubts.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Balanced Rock
passages.text:
I require peace to perform my meditation. Practice your arts while I meditate on Shu's location.

Other monks practice balance and combat upon the balance poles in the surrounding pools. Engage them and defeat them.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Balanced Rock
passages.text:
Even now, your skills increase. Your footing becomes more sure. Your blows strike with more force.

Discipline and practice are the keys to reaching our full potential.

passages.title: From Bad to Worse
passages.text:
After their ship crashed, evil creatures swept up from the sea to pick through the wreckage. Our aid may seem but a drop in the pond at the thought of the misfortune they've faced today.

Defeat their tormentors. These people desperately need our help.

passages.title: From Bad to Worse
passages.text: You are a fear to behold upon the battlefield.

passages.title: The Sting of Learning
passages.text:
There are dangers in the pools. The latest and most vicious are the water pincers. A time has come for their numbers to be diminished, and I am no longer up to the task.

If you could clear out some of the water pincers, I would be very appreciative. Beware their numbers... sometimes it's best to lure them from the pool-side rather than wading all the way in.

passages.title: The Sting of Learning
passages.text: The water pincers are strange creatures. They seem to be drawn to still water.

passages.title: The Sun Pearl
passages.text:
Shu, the spirit of water, is eternally young, as are all the spirits of Shen-zin Su. I have been friends with Shu all of my life, but I no longer have it within me to play with him. I am old, and lack the energy.

For all his complexities, Shu is simple to please: he desires friendship. When I returned to play with Shu each season, I would always bring a Sun Pearl as a gift, and then we would play together. You can find a Sun Pearl in the pools to the southeast. Perhaps you can be his new friend.

passages.title: The Sun Pearl
passages.text: The decision to not return to the pools was a hard one. I don't think Shu ever truly understood. He does not know what it is to get older and weaker.

passages.title: The Sun Pearl
passages.text:
Shu's desires are not so different from our own. He does not want to be alone. Unwanted, unloved. He longs to be needed, and to share his life with others.

Knowing that, earning his trust is not terribly difficult. He just wants company.

passages.title: Shu, the Spirit of Water
passages.text: Shu, the spirit of water, is sulking in the deep pool to the north. Cross the rocks and then drop the sun pearl in the center of the pool. He will know what this means.

passages.title: A New Friend
passages.text: He wants you to play with him. Go for it!

passages.title: A New Friend
passages.text: This is your task, <class>. See it through.

passages.title: A New Friend
passages.text:
I have to admit, that looked pretty fun from my angle.

And you seem to have made a new friend.

passages.title: Into the Mists
passages.text:
<Nazgrim fills his lungs with sea air.>

You smell that, <name>? It's the smell of our home, the lands our kind have bled and died to preserve.

And listen... you hear that? It's the sound of peace and safety - a haven we've carved, where our enemies fear to tread.

Remember these things. You won't experience them again anytime soon. We have ourselves a war to win.

Now go get settled, we're shovin' off!

passages.title: Into the Mists
passages.text:
<name>!?

They told me you were dead...

I'm glad to see it wasn't true. There's Alliance to kill!

passages.title: The General's Edge
passages.text:
As you gradually gather your senses and begin to take in your surroundings, this object stands out amongst the strewn wreckage.

It occurs to you that this is the first time you've seen Nazgrim's axe outside of his tight grasp. Somehow, this fact makes your predicament even more unsettling...

You know that dead or alive, the General would want his weapon back in his possession.

passages.title: My Stars!
passages.text:
A number of Kiryn's articles have been scattered around the area by wood sprites, but this one stands out as important to you.

The bag once hung from her waist, loaded with throwing stars. Without them, her arsenal will be considerably diminished.

If you were to retrieve the weapons from the pests that inhabit this region, it could only help your cause.

passages.title: Barrel of Monkies
passages.text: These monkeymen are driving me insane! I was just trying to get some insight into panderan brewing tactics and these hozu things keep drinking the brews before I can properly chemical test them. Can you please go take a few of them out as a lesson to the others? I'll make it worth your while.

passages.title: Kegplosion
passages.text:
Oh no <class>! In what can only be described as a contrived act of contention, the nearby spirit walkers have become enraged.

Please do something about them before they eat our faces!

passages.title: Horde Justice
passages.text:
Your mind races as you struggle to come to terms with your predicament - shipwrecked on an uncharted land, nearly all of the crew lost....

As you look at the corpse of this unfortunate creature you realize that the area is crawling with his kind, and that they're pillaging whatever supplies haven't been destroyed.

It's time to introduce these vermin to some good old-fashioned Horde justice.

passages.title: Standard Protocol
passages.text:
The Sky Shark has been totally destroyed.

With Alliance forces about, standard protocol requires the destruction of any sensitive technologies. These solenoids most certainly fall under that category.

The Horde's directives are clear, round up the solenoids for destruction.

passages.title: Wet Work!
passages.text:
If any Alliance naval forces have come ashore, the smoky fires from your crash will lead them right to you and what remains of your crew.

There must be a way to extinguish those flames...

This barrel seems to have survived the catastrophe intact. Perhaps it's still water-tight.

Only one way to find out!

passages.title: The Witch in the Woods
The Double Hozen Dare
passages.text:
There is a witch in the woods but no one believes me. She turned my friend Shin into jade!

We were all so scared we tried to run back but she sicced her big jade monsters on us. A bunch of my friends tried to get away by climbing trees.

Can you help me save my friends?

passages.title: The Double Hozen Dare
passages.text: Where is Shin? I didn't see Shin.

passages.title: The Double Hozen Dare
passages.text: Oh thank you so much for helping find my friends.  I still don't see Shin though...

passages.title: The Double Hozu Dare
passages.text:
Shin is still missing!

I never... I mean the other kids never should have double hozu dared him to knock on the witch's door. 

We saw a bunch of jade statues south of the Jade Witch's hut. 

Can you come with me and see if any of them are Shin?

passages.title: The Jade Witch
passages.text:
The Jade Witch must still have Shin.

I... I can't do it! I don't want to see the witch. Can you please go talk to her? You're an adult. I don't think she would turn you into jade.

passages.title: A Lesson in Bravery
The Jade Witch
passages.text:
The Jade Witch must still have Shin.

I... I can't do it! I don't want to see the witch. Can you please go talk to her and see if she has Shin?

You're an adult, I don't think she would try to turn you into jade.

passages.title: The Jade Witch
passages.text:
Hurray! Thank you so much! Shin is saved and you beat up the old witch! And the best part is our parents were never told what we were up to. Hurray!

It looks like everybody who came back are trying to get rid of whatever jade they had. Toya's been collecting it for some reason and said you should go chat with him.

passages.title: Burial at Sea
passages.text:
These savages are... ruthless.

They've dragged off our dying soldiers to be tormented in their camps. This is no way for our valiant brothers to die.

I shall join them soon enough, <class>. Please, put my mind at ease and their bodies to rest.

Find their remains at the camps surrounding the wreckage. Put them out of the reach of these creatures.

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Fire From the Sky
passages.text:
Yeah, we found Amber, she's alive, and all that. That's about where the good news stops though.

Let's see if I can pick up where ol' Rell left off...

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Fire From the Sky
passages.text: I'm not done with the report yet, <name>. Settle down.

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Fire From the Sky
passages.text:
So, now you know why ol' Rell's all beat up.

<You detect a change in Sully's facial expression, and he quickly turns away. Is he... crying?>

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Hostile Natives
passages.text: I... I can tell you what happened next! We continued north, into the forest...

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Hostile Natives
passages.text:
Luckily, we all made it out alive.

Well... all of us except for Socks...

passages.title: Without a Trace
passages.text: The explosives are set. All we have to do now is pull the trigger.

passages.title: Scouting Report: Hostile Natives
passages.text:
I bet I know your first question: "What the ook happened to Sergeant Gorrok?" Don't worry, don't worry. He's totally alive. Not dead or anything.

<Riko shuffles uncomfortably.>

Well, we THINK he's alive, but he ALSO might be very, very dead.

<Riko looks into your eyes for approval.>

Fine! Let me tell you exactly what happened.

passages.title: Scouting Report: Hostile Natives
passages.text: I'm not ookin' done yet!

passages.title: Scouting Report: Hostile Natives
passages.text: So, as you can see, none of this is Riko's fault.

passages.title: Scouting Report: On the Right Track
passages.text:
MOST of what Riko said is true.

We didn't dare pursue Gorrok - the Horde's numbers here are far too few. Our forces can only sustain so many losses, and frankly, we don't know how powerful that witch really is.

Let me pick up where the hozen left off...

passages.title: Scouting Report: On the Right Track
passages.text: If I may continue, please?

passages.title: Scouting Report: On the Right Track
passages.text:
And that's how we found our Alliance captive.

But that's not all that happened. Not by a long shot...

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Lost in the Woods
passages.text:
<Rell coughs heavily before speaking.>

Please, <name>. You need to hear what we've been through.

The whole damned Alliance needs to hear what we've been through. There may not be much time left.

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Lost in the Woods
passages.text: <Rell doesn't look too good. He should probably save his energy.>

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Lost in the Woods
passages.text:
...and that's <cough> how we found...

<Rell's speech devolves into heavy coughing. The corner of his mouth produces a trickle of blood.>

passages.title: Monstrosity
passages.text:
It's plain to see that this statue and the surrounding ruins are of ancient origin. Clearly, this land has a deep history, which means it could not have been born of the cataclysm.

And yet these waters have been explored for ages now, with no record of anything here but open sea.

Perhaps if you were to sketch the pieces of this broken statue, you might shed light on the continent's origins.

passages.title: Some "Pupil of Nature"
passages.text:
Wood sprites are not prone to wandering, so I'm surprised they ventured down as far as the mason's quarter. Something must be forcing them out of their natural habitat.

These particular sprites are native to the Woods of the Lost, just north of here. I'd go myself, but I've heard those woods are haunted.

So yeah, that's out.

I guess we'll never know.

<Weng coughs.>

Orrrr... A big brave adventurer like YOU could go check it out! What do you say?

passages.title: The Sprites' Plight
passages.text:
<Living statues rampage through the woods.

For now, they seem content in pummeling the forest sprites into splinters, but if they continue any further the pandaren will have more than just missing jade to worry about.>

passages.title: Breadcrumb Into Ruins
passages.text:
The spirits released from these statues are being pulled--rather violently--toward the coastal ruins up ahead.

It seems unlikely that they'll be allowed to rest...

passages.title: Break the Cycle
passages.text:
<Mogu conjurers call forth hapless spirits from beyond, forcing them into statues.

It seems that destroying the statues alone will not be enough to break the cycle.>

passages.title: Simulacrumble
passages.text:
<The shattered remains of an ancient mogu statue. This one looks like it never animated before it was broken.

Whatever dark magic the mogu are employing here, it seems to make the brittle statues significantly tougher. Better to destroy them while they are still vacant.

A good old-fashioned kick should do the job.>

passages.title: To Bridge Earth and Sky
passages.text:
We are ready to open the tan-chao and guide all of these spirits back to peace.

If I may, I would have your assistance once more. The mogu will surely sense the ritual taking place and will do everything in their power to halt it. I need only a few moments without interference, and once the path is open it will surge too greatly to be closed.

If you are willing to help one more time, please accompany me to the ritual site.

passages.title: Guess Whose Back
passages.text: <This dragon turtle's massive shell is rock-hard and covered in sharp ridges. One of the locals could almost certainly make use of it.>

passages.title: Guess Whose Back
passages.text:
My MY now look at THIS! What a beautiful shell!

You were wise to bring this to me, my friend. It will make a fantastic serving platter.

Please, take this for your troubles.

passages.title: Kung Din
passages.text:
I hope you are capable of this next task, for our lives depend on it.

There is only one key that will unlock our chains. Unfortunately, the key hangs around the neck of the hozen's pet tiger, Kung Din.

They keep the tiger in the great pit to the north. The only way to retrieve the key will be to kill the beast.

passages.title: Kung Din
passages.text: Did you find him?

passages.title: Kung Din
passages.text:
Yes, with this key I will be able to free our chains.

You have delivered us from this vile place.

passages.title: A Good Start
passages.text:
Regardless of our predicament, our orders stand. We are to learn the lay of this land and prepare it for Hellscream's fleet.

But first, we must deal with these savages!

You see these corpses I've stacked up around the camp? I want mountains of them!

We are the Horde!

These vermin have not learned to fear us yet, but we will fix that soon enough...

passages.title: Fish Fry
passages.text:
Fortune favors the bold!

Your calculated aggressive actions have yielded unexpected rewards. If you can slay these fishcatchers after a successful haul, you'll inherit their slippery spoils.

Thinning out the enemy while feeding your allies - the picture of efficiency!

passages.title: Rascals
passages.text:
I'll keep trying to find ways to wake this stubborn little guy up, but there is no shortage of trouble on the island it seems. The crops to the south are infested with virmen, rabbit-like thieves and pillagers.

Rascals!

They breed faster than we can kill them! I have the perfect solution for such a situation: kill them faster! With you here, <name>, that shouldn't be a problem.

passages.title: Rascals
passages.text: <name>, that's the way to do it! You show up, and problems start getting solved. That's just one of many reasons why I like you!

passages.title: Stronger Than Wood
passages.text:
Gather me wood planks from construction near the Ki-Han Brewery.

You do not yet know the extent of my strength, so I shall display it to you.

passages.title: Stronger Than Wood
passages.text: Have you done as I've asked?

passages.title: Stronger Than Wood
passages.text:
Good.

My head, it is harder than the densest wood.

Step back, and let me dispel your doubts.

passages.title: Raucous Rousing
passages.text:
You ready for this, <name>? I'm thinking maybe we should have looked for something to cover our ears, but it's a bit late for that now. Just remember that the intense ringing you'll be hearing for the next few hours is the ringing sound of victory!

The honor's all yours, <name>. Ring the gong whenever you're ready!

passages.title: Raucous Rousing
passages.text:
Huh... well... that's definitely the ringing I expected, but I was hoping for a bit more from Wugou. This guy's a deep sleeper, that's for sure.

It's alright, <name>. I've got another idea, and there's not much preparation needed at all - just how I like it.

passages.title: Wugou, the Spirit of Earth
passages.text:
<name>! Well, the plus side is that finding Wugou was easy enough. Waking him... not so much. I think he's going to wake quite sore from all the pushing and hitting I've done trying to rouse him.

Are you a deep sleeper at all, <name>? What wakes you up in the morning?

Rolling out of bed always seems to do it for me, so I figure let's just go for that! I tied off some ropes to the ox cart. We send it running and give him a good roll, and we should be good! Care to give the ox a good slap to get it going?

passages.title: Morning Breeze Village
passages.text:
The fourth and final spirit is Dafeng, the spirit of air. When he is not in the skies, he can be found on the Ridge of Laughing Winds to the west. I've sent both Aysa and Ji to help you find him.

When you are ready, I will summon winds to carry you to the top of the temple. From there, cross the bridges to the west and find Ji in Morning Breeze Village.

passages.title: Morning Breeze Village
passages.text:
<name>, give me a hug! Our parting was not so long this time - I quite prefer it that way!

You've been working with Aysa, have you not? Our disciplines have always kept us apart, so I know little of her. Watching her perform her exercises now, I must confess that she possesses a grace and discipline that is strangely alluring.

There are more pressing thoughts though, aren't there? <name>, let's take care of this monkey problem while we search for Dafeng.

passages.title: Tools of the Enemy
passages.text: The hozen have stolen our brushes and are painting over our scrolls of wisdom with their own wisdoms, if you can call them that. If you're here to help, stop them and bring our brushes back before they can do more harm.

passages.title: Tools of the Enemy
passages.text: I do not wish to disparage the hozen for their aspirations - each race must walk its own path. In this moment, however, they are bringing harm to our bodies and our culture. That is a line that cannot be crossed.

passages.title: Tools of the Enemy
passages.text: I am very thankful, young one. I will soon begin the slow task of documenting all of our wisdoms again, so that the scrolls can be hung for the benefit of all to come.

passages.title: Rewritten Wisdoms
passages.text:
<name>, we must help Elder Shaopai. There are few more deserving of our kindness.

On the way here, you surely noticed the scrolls of wisdom hanging in the grotto to the south. The hozen have defiled many of them, and sadly, they are not recoverable. We will deal with the problem directly - burn the defiled scrolls. Wipe the hozen writings away entirely.

Do not worry for Elder Shaopai. The people shall come together and help him rewrite the wisdoms in time. I shall see to that.

passages.title: Rewritten Wisdoms
passages.text: You're a good man, <name>. You have proven that again and again, and I am glad to stand beside you.

passages.title: The Direct Solution
passages.text:
Alright <name>, this is the second time we've had to deal with ravaging hozen. I think it's time we take care of this problem the Huojin way. No more patience. No more mediation. We go to the source.

We're going into the hozen village to the north and we're punishing those smelly troublemakers. I've been looking forward to a chance to fight by your side again, <name>.

passages.title: The Direct Solution
passages.text: Invigorating! A good fight always makes me feel better!

passages.title: Do No Evil
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to understand that the way of the Huojin is not the way of violence. When fighting is needed, we will not hesitate, but when fighting is not needed, neither do we instigate. However, the direct solution is often cutting the head off the snake, as they say.

The hozen have a leader instigating these attacks. If we remove Ruk-Ruk, we won't have to wipe the hozen out entirely.

I know you are not of the Huojin, but are you with me in what must be done, <name>?

passages.title: Do No Evil
passages.text: <name>, I think you've got a bit of Huojin in you. Stick with me and I'll bring you around, I think.

passages.title: Monkey Advisory Warning
passages.text:
The monkeys have been stealing from the village during their attacks. We should be fine without some of the extra food stores, but the idea of monkeys with fireworks... I'm a little bit concerned. Not to mention, who knows when some fireworks will come in handy?

Help me recover the stolen fireworks from their village, <name>?

passages.title: Monkey Advisory Warning
passages.text: I'm somewhat impressed they hadn't set their village on fire with these things.

passages.title: Monkey Advisory Warning
passages.text: <name>, I'm thinking we should celebrate with these later. What do you think?

passages.title: Stronger Than Stone
passages.text:
Gather me stone blocks from the Ridge of Laughing Winds to the south.

You have seen my strength twice, yet I still spy doubt within your eyes. It will not last.

passages.title: Stronger Than Stone
passages.text: The strength of the body cannot exist without the strength of the mind.

passages.title: Stronger Than Stone
passages.text:
Good.

My head, it is harder than the strongest stone.

Step back, and let me dispel your doubts.

passages.title: Worthy of Passing
passages.text:
The four elemental spirits will help you speak with the land and uncover its plight, but first, I have one small task to ask of you.

Join me, my pupil. Accompany this old pandaren to the western grove.

passages.title: Worthy of Passing
passages.text: I do not have the strength of body or will that I once did. I'm glad there are noble <race> like you to fight on for our people. You've come far, <name>.

passages.title: Unwelcome Nature
passages.text:
You faced forest sprites in the Dawning Valley, but the forest sprites in this grove are a different breed. Crueler and more dangerous.

If you would clear some of these sprites out, the spirits would thank you.

passages.title: Unwelcome Nature
passages.text: The spirits thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Small, But Significant
passages.text:
I am tired, <name>. I must rest.

We have a ritual to perform, but we require some of the charms from this grove. If you wander the grove, you should see them all over hanging from the trees. 

If it does not offend one as young as you, will you permit me to sit and recover my strength while you gather these charms?

passages.title: Small, But Significant
passages.text: Rest feels good. The burdens of life have become a great weight after so many years.

passages.title: Small, But Significant
passages.text: You come through, as you always have. You are truly one of my greatest students. I think you will be something the likes of which the world has never seen.

passages.title: Passing Wisdom
passages.text: This journey shall soon be yours to undertake without me. Stay for a few moments and listen to an old man's words. Let my knowledge serve as a foundation for yours, that you might be greater than I ever was.

passages.title: Passing Wisdom
passages.text: I know, <name>... I know. Such is the way of things.

passages.title: The Suffering of Shen-zin Su
passages.text:
Now is not the time to grieve. The balloon is ready, and Shen-zin Su awaits.

We shall be the first pandaren to speak to Shen-zin Su in hundreds of years. It is a great honor.

passages.title: The Suffering of Shen-zin Su
passages.text: You have undergone a great honor, <class>. Have you come back wiser for it?

passages.title: Bidden to Greatness
passages.text:
It is up to all of you to remove the thorn from the side of Shen-zin Su. Do not let your differences come between you. Trust in each other.

Within the Pei-Wu Forest is a lone hermit. Head directly to his hut. He knows intimately of the dark things that now lurk in the trees.

passages.title: Bidden to Greatness
passages.text:
Evil is rising from the seas and filling the forest. It's not just tigers anymore... something far more sinister lurks in the shadows, waiting to take any <race> unwise enough to stray out alone.

You are not safe here.

passages.title: Evil from the Seas
passages.text: I do not know what this evil is that is infesting the forest, <name>, but I know exactly how to deal with it. So do you, I think.

passages.title: Evil from the Seas
passages.text: You make me proud, <name>. You make all of us proud.

passages.title: None Left Behind
passages.text:
Your friend has been doing everything she can to save my crew. I'm deeply appreciative.

We're still dealing with more than we can handle here: quenching the fires on the wreckage, getting my people out, fighting off these evil sea creatures, and trying to prevent the prisoners from escaping. We're simply in over our heads.

I still have men on the ship that we need to get clear before the wreckage collapses on them. I know this is asking a lot, but can you help?

passages.title: None Left Behind
passages.text: I have no idea who you people are, but fate surely smiled on us this day. Many more would be dead if not for the help of you and your friends. I am in your debt.

passages.title: Stocking Stalks
passages.text:
My men are malnourished, injured, and exhausted, but they are Horde. Every one will fight to their dying breath. As our new ally, we will stand by you when the time comes, but we would stand stronger with weapons.

I have my men out gathering bamboo stalks to fashion into spears. If you can spare the effort, we could use the extra pair of capable hands.

passages.title: Stocking Stalks
passages.text: The Horde does not back down from a fight.

passages.title: Stocking Stalks
passages.text: These are excellent! We'll have them crafted into weapons in no time.

passages.title: Medical Supplies
passages.text: We need supplies to tend to our wounded, but the supply crates containing them were scattered in the crash. If you can bring back any crates you find, I would be very grateful.

passages.title: Medical Supplies
passages.text: Did you find the boxes I spoke of?

passages.title: Medical Supplies
passages.text:
These will do perfectly. I'll get my medics to work immediately.

Thank you.

passages.title: An Ancient Evil
passages.text:
<name>, I was looking for you!

One of the escaping sailors just spotted Aysa in the wreckage of the ship, facing some enormous beast. She might need your help - you should go to her, quickly!

passages.title: An Ancient Evil
passages.text:
<Aysa is clearly exhausted from the fight.>

Your skills in battle... are unquestionable... <class>.

Did you save the escaped prisoners?  ...Where is Ji? Is he okay?

passages.title: The Wanderer
Efficient Excavations
passages.text:
This manual describes outlandish theories on how to most efficiently manage large groups of workers as they engage in massive excavation projects.

After a quick skim of the material, it becomes clear to you that the author of the book is the figure in charge of the over-aggressive pillagers here.

A map on the back cover indicates that the author has a bunker in the southwest region of Uldum.

Perhaps an introduction is in order.

passages.title: Save the Cuddlies
passages.text:
The Fox Grove has become a dangerous place for the local red pandas. 

Sadly due to my actions helping that crazy Brewmaster Shadowpour, the foxes of the grove have developed an inebriation bite. The result is the little red pandas keep getting drunk until they can no longer defend themselves. 

Please! Can you help me?

If you round up some of them I have an aroma about this fire that will help sober them up. That should keep them safe for at least a short while.

passages.title: Lethal Hangovers
passages.text:
I told him not to do it! But "no one stands in the way of Brewmaster Shadowpour".

My master went and contaminated the local water supply trying to "add flavor" to the water. The toxins trickled down here to the Fox Grove where the brew has an irreversible effect on the foxes. 

It warps their minds and sends them into a frenzy. Now they are a permanent danger to any travelers and local wildlife.

Can you help me cull some of their numbers please?

passages.title: Need a Chaser
passages.text:
It appears now that my master managed to poison the entire local water supply with his flavor experiments.

I might have a treatment but need some supplies. In lighter cases my people have found orchids to be a wonderful remedy.

Defeat the orchid chasers in the Orchis Hollow and collect some of the pollinated orchids they carry. We will use them to cleanse the central water source.

passages.title: Forensic Science
passages.text:
These creatures are everywhere - and very hostile! We'll need to deal with them before any more Alliance show up.

This one's taken quite a beating, but I've still made some determinations about its anatomy.

With the proper reagents, I'll be able to fashion a poison that should be quite effective against this species. In fact, I'll just need to modify a bit of the poison I have with me.

Go and find me some viscous chlorophyll down by the water. Any semi-sentient flora should do.

passages.title: Forensic Science
passages.text: I hope you were successful. Our survival here may depend on it.

passages.title: Forensic Science
passages.text: Oh, yes, <name>. This will do nicely.

passages.title: Drunken Tigers
passages.text:
Orchids may be the cure for my people, but they are an intense opiate for the local tigers. These beasts are often drawn to orchid fields and the intoxicating effects the flowers have on them.

When you add the toxins Shadowpour introduced to the water supply it results in very dangerous and rabid animals. It won't be long before they are threatening the Jade Temple. 

Can you thin some of their numbers please?

passages.title: The New Master
passages.text:
I figured it out! With the toxins you provided I not only recreated Shadowpour's recipe but also fixed the problem he was having that was causing illness.

Do you know what this means? All that flavor and none of the lethal side effects!

Now to deal with the Brewmaster. I've loaded up Chalky with samples. Can you take these to challenge Shadowpour to a tasters' duel?

You'll be subjected to his brews but I will help you cheat by bringing my sobering fire.

passages.title: Missed Me By... That Much!
passages.text:
Listen, <pal/toots>.

I sent out a coupla supply drones from the gunship, and they've all been lost or crashed. Almost all, that is.

One of 'em buzzed right through the camp here and crashed out by them waterfalls.

How 'bout you see what you can do about bringin' the contents of that crate back here, hmm?

We're all outta drones, but my rocket boots might yet come in handy... or footy, as the case may be.

Hah! I just kill me...

passages.title: Missed Me By... That Much!
passages.text: This crate should be full of supplies...

passages.title: Scouting Report: The Friend of My Enemy
passages.text:
We weren't only looking for Alliance, you know. We were also looking for those snooked-up, tik-flikklin' jinyu!

Well, we found 'em all right...

passages.title: Scouting Report: The Friend of My Enemy
passages.text: Riko wishes you were a bit more patient, <name>.

passages.title: Scouting Report: The Friend of My Enemy
passages.text:
Yeah, I ran away. So blikkin' what? If it weren't for me, Kiryn would be dead. Oh, wait... she's already dead... already...

Go away! Riko's head hurts.

passages.title: Sacred Scroll
passages.text:
The unfamiliar markings on this parchment have an elegance about them that Yoggtord and his gang don't seem capable of.

You suspect that, like everything else these Hozu possess, this is stolen merchandise.

Perhaps the original owner of the scroll is still nearby...

passages.title: Lay of the Land[TEMP]
passages.text:
Grah!!

For every one of these muck-flingers we kill, another two spring from the woods to take its place. I wouldn't share this with the others, but it's clear that we won't last long here, <name>.

I must stay and defend what remains of our belongings. You scout out the region and seek a solution to our primate problem.

Go now. Our hope goes with you...

passages.title: Seeking Answers
passages.text:
<Cho endures your stream of questions before speaking.>

So much to ponder, traveler...

You first must learn how to ask before your mind can discern the truth.

I have completed my meditations for today, but my candles remain at the Cairn of Blood.

Go there. Clear your mind. We will speak again when you are prepared to hear my words.

passages.title: Aunty Lin Windfur
passages.text:
We will start heading back to town once everyone gets organized. No way is anyone going to mess with me now! I'll boot them in the head! I'm sure I won't be in trouble after this.

Thank you so much for your help. Can you tell Aunty Lin back in Panda Town that we are okay and on our way back? She has tons of old cool stuff she might give you as a reward.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: Claiming Kalimdor
passages.text:
Victory shall soon be ours! Our forces have engaged the enemy all over Kalimdor.

Warchief Garrosh Hellscream has commanded all able-bodied <race>s to report for duty in support of our latest offensive.

Make your way to Grommash Hold in Orgrimmar and present yourself to General Nazgrim for immediate assignment! For the Horde!

passages.title: Cairn of Bone
passages.text:
Your mind felt clear.

You thought you were focused.

Maybe it was the droning of the nearby insects that put you to sleep. That must've been it!

Out of the corner of your eye, you see another of the stone formations just north of here.

Perhaps it's quieter at that one...

passages.title: Wisdom of the Ages
passages.text:
You must learn to approach your life's trials with humility and an open mind, stranger.

Wisdom cannot fit through the narrow slits of the skeptic's eye.

Meet me at the Cairn of Stone and I shall teach you the ancient art of meditation.

Once you are at peace, you may find that the answers you seek are not as distant as you might think them to be.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: Spies in Our Midst
passages.text:
This is unacceptable! The warchief needs every ship he can get to secure Kalimdor!

How DID the night elves find out about the new fleet in time to destroy it? There's only one way...

Orgrimmar is full of the enemy's eyes and ears, <name>, and it is our job to root them out. Belloc Brightblade has provided me with a tool that he says can help reveal the spies.

Use it, but don't trust it alone. Use your judgment.

passages.title: One Hand Clapping
passages.text:
You have much yet to learn, but your feet are now on the path to enlightenment.

Take what I have taught you here and apply it at the lake to the west.

With patience and practice, harmony and enlightenment can be attained. Then, wisdom will flow freely into your mind.

Also, you will be far enough away that your snoring will not interfere with my own studies.

Farewell, stranger.

passages.title: Clever Ashyo
passages.text:
I'm not sure where Clever Ashyo got his "Clever" title from. All jinyu are clever, and I wouldn't say that he's any more clever than most of them.

Quite the opposite, actually.

At least he's a capable fighter. He did well enough at Tian Monastery to be selected for our training mission.

If you want to help him look for the Hidden Master, you can find him along the Valley's northern border.

passages.title: Clever Ashyo
passages.text: Where have I seen you before?

passages.title: Lin Tenderpaw
passages.text:
Lin is more talented than she thinks she is. Strong of fist but weak of spirit. With more confidence, she could be better than all of us.

Perhaps she will find the surety she needs on her trip into the west. She's probably on her way to Stoneplow as we speak. Stop and speak to her, if you find yourself on that side of the Valley.

passages.title: Lin Tenderpaw
passages.text:
Oh, it's you!

No, I haven't found the Hidden Master yet. I probably wasted my time coming out here.

<Sigh...>

passages.title: Ken-Ken
passages.text:
So... Ken-Ken. The hozen.

Personally, I'm impressed he's progressed so far in his training. He's got a brain between his ears, which is more than can be said for most of his kind.

He said he was headed east, but, seeing as we're already on the far east side of the valley, I can't imagine he went too far from here. Look for him at Zhu's Watch, in Krasarang Wilds, down the path to the south. See what he's found.

passages.title: Ken-Ken
passages.text:
This place... it... it so SAD!

Ken-Ken never seen a place so sad.

passages.title: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text:
Kang's pride regularly becomes overconfidence, which often leads him down dangerous paths. His current path is as dangerous as any - he is headed deep into the Krasarang Wilds.

I wouldn't normally ask a favor of a stranger, but... would you make sure that he is well? It would give me relief to know that a brave <race> was looking out for him.

passages.title: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text: I'm pretty sure this settlement wasn't here a few weeks ago. Where did these people come from?

passages.title: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text:
Kang's pride regularly becomes overconfidence, which often leads him down dangerous paths. His current path is as dangerous as any - he is headed deep into the Krasarang Wilds.

I wouldn't normally ask a favor of a stranger, but... would you make sure that he is well? It would give me relief to know that a brave <race> was looking out for him.

passages.title: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text: I'm pretty sure this settlement wasn't here a few weeks ago. Where did these people come from?

passages.title: Building a Better Hozen Trap
passages.text:
One thing is now painfully clear. The Hozen love their 'slickies'.

While deep in your meditative trance, scattered images and impressions came to your mind. Now fully awake, you struggle to make sense of the experience.

The beginnings of an absurd plan begin to take shape in your head. It might just be crazy enough to work...

passages.title: Tracking Event: Spies Leave
passages.text:
It's time for Sully and I to leave. We'll keep our eyes out for any sign of the White Pawn and report back shortly.

I'm afraid I must leave you in charge while Admiral Taylor is recovering. Learn as much as you can from these jinyu while we are away. I expect a full report when we return.

passages.title: Road Rations
passages.text:
We do not have time to wait around for the Admiral to recover.

Sully and I are planning to search for Anduin to the north, but we'll need supplies for our journey.

The lake here is teeming with wildlife, which we have received permission to hunt.

Go and gather some supplies while Sully and I finalize our preparations.

passages.title: Road Rations
passages.text:
Time is short. Each hour we delay, the White Pawn may move further away.

Where are the supplies I asked for?

passages.title: Road Rations
passages.text: This should be plenty, <name>. Thanks.

passages.title: Zen Healing
passages.text:
Your friend Taylor is in critical shape. Unfortunately, his wounds are tainted by hozen poison, which is very difficult to cure.

Luckily, through many generations of fighting the hozen, my people have developed medicines to treat such injuries.

The flowers growing on the surface of Glass Lake are needed to make the antidote.

<name>, go quickly and bring back some blooms. Your Admiral's life depends on it.

passages.title: Borrowed Brew
passages.text:
A delicious smell wafts out from the bottle on the table.

A little taste couldn't hurt, right?

passages.title: Borrowed Brew
passages.text:
I heard your people had washed up on our shores, but I did not expect to find one washed up on my very doorstep! What brings you here, stranger?

<You explain about your search for Prince Anduin, and describe the boy to the pandaren.>

Very interesting! And so the Pearlfin sent you to me, did they?

passages.title: Body
passages.text:
A brew's body is an important and often overlooked factor.

To create the perfect consistency, I will need pristine eyes from the Bog Crocolisks to the east.

Take care. The creatures are quite vicious.

passages.title: Body
passages.text: Watch your step in the swamp, my new friend.

passages.title: Body
passages.text: Do you have crocolisks where you are from?

passages.title: Hue
passages.text:
The most distinguishing feature of the Dream Brew is its iridescent, dream-like color.

To the east, you will find Glittering Amberflies. I will need their wings to create the final luminescent color of the brew.

Take this knife and use it to collect 8 wings.

passages.title: Hue
passages.text: Have you collected all the ingredients? It is almost time to make the Dream Brew.

passages.title: Hue
passages.text:
Beautiful color, rare transparency, shimmer but not sparkle...these will do quite well.

I am beginning to see great potential in you, strange one.

passages.title: Trail of the White Pawn
passages.text:
Although the cloak is ragged and torn, there is no mistaking the fine tailoring and the King's royal crest.

You should show it to your Alliance commander.

passages.title: Trail of the White Pawn
passages.text:
This is Anduin's cloak, <name>!

This must mean he passed through this forest.

We must heighten our efforts to find him.

passages.title: Steaking a Claim
passages.text:
Since we're already out here, no sense in going back empty-handed, right?

Now, did you know that the porcupines around these parts have just about the rarest, juiciest steak a person has ever tasted?

They're difficult to hunt because of their sharp spikes, but you look like you can handle your own.

Go on and round me up a couple of steaks to take back to camp.

We may be roughing it out in this wilderness, but we can still eat like kings!

passages.title: No Such Thing As A Free Lunch
passages.text:
The fighting's over, but we're not out of trouble yet. Not by a long shot.

Our camp is falling dangerously low on supplies, but our provisioner didn't make it back from the battle.

Some of the troops saw her being dragged into the forest to the north.

Please, would you find her?

passages.title: Rest in Peace
passages.text:
The spirits... the cavedwellers... they howl in agony... 

Trapped... in this world... cannot move... to the next.

I... will go mad... listening... to their cries... 

Please...go...put them to rest.

passages.title: Rest in Peace
passages.text: Thank you... friend. I am... happy... knowing... the spirits... are at peace.

passages.title: Anduin's Decision
passages.text:
You have done all you can for the Prince's friends.

You completed your mission and found the White Pawn - Prince Anduin. Admiral Taylor and the other SI:7 agents will be eager to have the boy safe in their custody.

It is time to return home.

passages.title: Anduin's Decision
passages.text:
He did WHAT?!?!?

He's lucky that I haven't found him yet, because when I do, I just might kill him myself!

Whatever he thinks he's doing... chasing after this Vale... it is not behavior fit for a prince!

If we didn't have more pressing matters at hand, I would send our entire fleet chasing after his heels!

passages.title: Fighting the Flames
passages.text:
Those monkeys seem to be more savage than intelligent, but they're smart enough to know that fire is a powerful weapon.

I don't need to explain that if those fires are left unchecked, they'll destroy everything we've built here.

All my men have their hands full, so you'll have to do it. Take this bucket of water and put out those flames!

passages.title: Let Them Burn
passages.text:
Advance scouts report that the hozen at the Slingtail Pits are amassing with reinforcements from their tribes to the north.

Our forces are gathered for battle on the ridge to the northwest. They are just waiting for you.

Now is the time to show them what we are made of. Now is the time to destroy them indefinitely.

passages.title: Let Them Burn
passages.text: The waters were right about you, <name>. Because of your efforts, this village has a future. We will not forget the lessons you've taught us, <class>.

passages.title: Carp Diem
passages.text:
Despite the hozen's apparent disarray, there is an order to their chaos. Their leader, Chief Gukgut, is the shrewd mastermind behind their attacks.

He is organizing their movements at the great pit at the hozen camp to the northwest.

Strike now and show him no mercy, <name>, for he will do the same.

passages.title: Carp Diem
passages.text:
Without their leader, these hozen should once again settle into disarray.

Today we rejoice in our victory! <name>, you came to us a stranger, but you depart as a friend.

From henceforth, you are the highest of the high - a valued friend and defender of the Pearlfin tribe.

passages.title: Chen and Li Li
passages.text:
My niece and I are new to Pandaria. Probably like yourself. We're visitors from the Wandering Isle, and, to be honest, we have no idea where we're going.

That farm up ahead looks as fine a place as any to take off our shoes and enjoy a brew. What do you say, Li Li?

<race>? Would you like to share the road with us?

passages.title: Chen and Li Li
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Chen and Li Li
passages.text:
Welcome, welcome, visitors! You've come to sample some of my son's turnips? Perhaps purchase a few pigs?

Please, make yourselves at home. I have plenty of room.

passages.title: Low Turnip Turnout
passages.text:
Your help here is appreciated, <name>. I'd like to give you another job, if you're interested.

My son, Ang, runs the small farm just down this hill. He should have brought me some fruits and vegetables this morning, but I haven't seen him all day.

Would you go down there and see what's going on?

passages.title: Low Turnip Turnout
passages.text:
Wha-? Who the...? My father sent you?

Pshh... he can be so nosy sometimes. I have everything under control here.

passages.title: Back to the Sty
passages.text:
I try to keep an eye on my stock, but every once in a while some of them sneak away. With all the confusion these virmen are causing, I may have let my guard down for a few moments, and some of my pigs escaped.

Care to look for them? I'd start by looking down the hill, to the west.

passages.title: Back to the Sty
passages.text: Have you found them? There should be three missing, I think.

passages.title: Back to the Sty
passages.text:
There they are! Back into the sty with you three, now!

<Liang looks up at you.>

Thank you, neighbor. I'm truly grateful for your assistance.

passages.title: Piercing Talons and Slavering Jaws
passages.text:
First the hawks came. You've probably seen some of them circling up above.

The wolves came shortly after. I think they smelled my weakness.

I'm not nearly as brave as Master Shang thought I was. The master will be quite cross with me if I don't do something about these beasts.

Can... can you help, <sir/ma'am>?

passages.title: Piercing Talons and Slavering Jaws
passages.text: I wish I were brave enough to fight them, but...

passages.title: Piercing Talons and Slavering Jaws
passages.text: They... they're not stopping, but at least we fought back. Right?

passages.title: Lupello
passages.text:
I've been thinking... the wolves might stop attacking if we kill their pack leader.

We call him Lupello, and he patrols the opposite riverbank.

<Francis' concentration is broken by another attack. Perhaps you should go deal with Lupello yourself.>

passages.title: Lupello
passages.text: What will Master Shang say when he finds out?

passages.title: Lupello
passages.text: I know I should be the one fighting them off. Maybe I'm not cut out for shepherding after all.

passages.title: The Dream Brew
passages.text:
The Dream Brew is ready.

Drink it at the Seer's Stone, just to the right of the red pagoda.

Seek, and find.

passages.title: Kill Kher Shan
passages.text:
Kher Shan is one big dooker.

Grooked all my sons! Ick Ick, Nab Nab, Eet Eet, Bitty Bitty, and the others I can't remember.

Wikket wanna help hozen? Go grook Kher Shan!

The dooker's over there.

<Nibi Nibi points to the east.>

passages.title: Mann's Man
passages.text:
<For once, the foreman lowers her voice.>

Look, this ain't easy... I got another favor to ask. My idiot husband, Hao, is a shift lead down at the quarry. I told him not to go back, that it was too dangerous, but he's as stubborn as a hozen and twice as stupid. Says the boys need him around for "moral support."

<Mann sneers.>

What about my moral support?! What am I gonna do if that idiot dies?!

Please... keep an eye out for him. Tell him to come home.

<Her eyes soften before she turns away.>

passages.title: Mann's Man
passages.text:
<Hao looks up at you, struggling to pull himself from the rubble.>

No, no. I got it. HNNGHHH!!

Okay, maybe I don't got it.

passages.title: Trapped!
passages.text:
<Hao struggles against the rubble with all his might.>

HNNNGHHH!!

Let me guess: my wife sent you? Imagine that, my delicate little snow lily all worried. Ha ha! She's always frettin' over me. Look--HNNGHH!!!--it'll take more than a little--HNNGGHHH!!--cave-in to keep ol' Hao down.

Some o' the boys, on the other hand, are in trouble. Help 'em out if you find any, will ya? I'll be fine.

Really.

passages.title: Trapped!
passages.text:
<Hao lets out a hearty laugh.>

I seen 'em come runnin' out o' there like ol' Kher Shan himself were givin' chase.

passages.title: The Bees' Knees
passages.text:
You really hozen friend, wikket? Let's see, hmm?

Hozen at Grookin' Hill all outta slicky bait. Tigerflies' legs stay twitchy in water - make best bait!

Bo Bo sick from stings. Wikket get bait and take to Grookin.

passages.title: The Bees' Knees
passages.text: Slicky food!

passages.title: The Bees' Knees
passages.text: Woot! Woot! Wikket da Ook Dook!

passages.title: Orders are Orders
passages.text:
Hmm, maybe wikket not so bad after all!

Other baldskins not nice to hozen.

Hozen take this from bad wikkets!

All wikket loot goes to Kah Kah - Chief's orders!
