We were laying an ambush for the Alliance in the ruins west of here when the mogu ambushed us. They are using mage portals to call in reinforcements.

passages.title: Going on the Offensive
passages.text:
Ha! So my father just wasted twenty years of our lives on a fool's errand!

I'm taking charge.

When Tyrande sent us here she was very specific that we not come back until we find the source of the Light that she saw in her visions. It's obvious now that the Pools of Youth were not it.

We are pressing westward and could use your help.

Meet us at the Sentinel Basecamp further west when you are ready.

passages.title: Going on the Offensive
passages.text: <name>, well timed as usual. It turns out the mogu know how to use portals as well.

passages.title: Sufficient Motivation
passages.text:
Training these savages has been quite a task, <name>.

Finding ways to motivate them was easy enough; the problem is keeping them motivated.. and focused... and awake.

Now that you're back, you can help me in getting the less disciplined Hozen moving, if you catch my drift. I'll leave the method up to you.

passages.title: Sufficient Motivation
passages.text: Are the Hozen ready to deploy?

passages.title: Sufficient Motivation
passages.text:
Hrmm, I'll be surprised if we can keep these creatures focused enough to employ any tactics at all, <name>.

They'd better not get in my way when blades begin to fly!

passages.title: My Son...
passages.text:
My son - can you find my son?

When the Jinyu attacked, he ran off in the confusion. I don't know if they've done anything with him, or if he's still alive, even.

Nothing else matters if I can't find him. 

I'd ask Mei... but something's wrong with her. She seems too... impulsive since the attack. I just can't trust that she'd bring him back safely.

passages.title: My Son...
passages.text: So horrible... When I saw the killing, I just ran. My father, Mei... are they alive?

passages.title: Repossession
passages.text:
Of course, the first priority is finding my son. But, if we save ourselves only to starve, then what have we accomplished, in the end?

Please, I need you to recover some of the supplies that the Jinyu took from our caravan.

passages.title: Repossession
passages.text: Have you found the supplies?

passages.title: Repossession
passages.text: Thank you... we will eat now, at least.

passages.title: The Ritual
passages.text:
From the moment I first rose from the river, I knew I was destined to be Waterspeaker.

I was taught many rituals, and have performed all of them, save one.

There was one, an extremely ancient one, that we were told to call upon if our people ever turned against us. 

This must have happened in our people's distant past, because we haven't needed to use it in our village's memory.

I suppose now is the time to do so.

passages.title: The Ritual
passages.text: That... was not what I expected.

passages.title: The Ritual
passages.text: I see now that this ritual rips whatever was controlling the minds of these creatures from them. I now know what we must do.

passages.title: Carved in Stone
passages.text:
You see the shiny stones in the walls? Rook wants some. The mogu been collecting them, so they have some to take too maybe.

If you find stones, you please bring them to Rook? Rook will be your friend.

passages.title: Carved in Stone
passages.text: You find stones for Rook? Please?

passages.title: Carved in Stone
passages.text:
So many!  And so shiny! You did real good!

Thank you, little friend. Rook like you a lot.

passages.title: Comin' Round the Mountain
passages.text:
The mountain pass is very dangerous. You need much luck to survive. Nephew Bentnail will show you the way.

Perhaps today is a lucky day to travel though. Wind blows from the east; this is good sign. Grummles always travel best when east wind blows.

Climb in the cart when you are ready to leave.

passages.title: Comin' Round the Mountain
passages.text: You must be very lucky to survive the pass!

passages.title: Comin' Round the Mountain
passages.text: You've arrived just in time, <class>! I was starting to think I would die up here!

passages.title: The Missing Muskpaw
passages.text:
What the heck are you supposed to be? |5<class>? Never heard of one of them. You here to help or to steal my yaks?

Look, if yer' insistin' on helpin' out, go find my boy. He got himself grabbed by a bunch of sprites and probably doesn't even know we lost the ranch.

They dragged him off to Pranksters' Hollow south east of here. Go rescue him an' I'll see about giving you a reward of some sort.

passages.title: The Missing Muskpaw
passages.text: Thank you for the save, stranger!

passages.title: Yakity Yak
passages.text:
Yaungols! They come through here taking what they want and destroying whatever's left.

I can't have these thugs destroy the last pieces of the Yak Wash here. It's all my boy and I have left.

Head over to our old ranch and dish out some pain on them yaungols. I bet if you kill enough of them they'll think twice before attacking anything in this area.

passages.title: Get Back Here!
passages.text:
Oh, before I forget, I have something I was asked to deliver to you. A letter from one of your companions, I assume.

I was made to understand that your presence was urgently required, so I took the liberty of arranging your passage.

Speak to Ginsa Arroweye just south of here when you're ready. She has a kite waiting.

passages.title: Get Back Here!
passages.text: Welcome back, <name>. I trust your journey has been insightful, particularly in regards to the layout of the land. There is still much to do before we march into battle.

passages.title: Get Back Here!
passages.text:
Oh, before I forget, I have something I was asked to deliver to you. A letter from one of your companions, I assume.

I was made to understand that your presence was urgently required, so I took the liberty of arranging your passage.

Speak to Ginsa Arroweye just south of here when you're ready. She has a kite waiting.

passages.title: Get Back Here!
passages.text:
Throm-Ka, <name>!

I hope you were able to gather useful information while on your journey through the forest.

Our preperations are almost complete, but your help is needed.

passages.title: Residual Fallout
passages.text:
Pandaria is a mystical land, traveler.

It bears repeating that some of its secrets remain hidden, even to Lorewalkers.

Sealing those fissures did not mend what has been broken. If the legends are true, it will take much more to release this land from the grasp of the Sha.

The aggression of that battle awakened a host of living negative emotions. What you see here is likely the first of many such manifestations.

For now, we can only try to diminish their presence here.

passages.title: Residual Fallout
passages.text: This, it seems, is only the tip of the iceberg, <name>.

passages.title: Residual Fallout
passages.text:
This is terrible...

We must find a way to undo what has been done here.

passages.title: Jaded Heart
passages.text:
The more powerful remnants of that horrible manifestation may be too much for you to handle on your own, <name>.

I fear I'd be of little help in terms of actual combat, but I can suggest a solution.

The great jade statue was soon to become a living serpent - one of our revered celestials. Its construction imbued it with special powers that may sufficiently weaken these adversaries.

passages.title: Jaded Heart
passages.text: Do you have the jade, <name>?

passages.title: Jaded Heart
passages.text:
<Cho looks at you despondently.>

This jade was meant for... so much more.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your Admiral Taylor has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs in the apothecary's house across the way.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
<name>, is that you? I can't believe we survived the destruction of the Jade Serpent.

Some of us anyway.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your Admiral Taylor has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
<name>, is that you? I can't believe we survived the destruction of the Jade Serpent.

Some of us anyway.

passages.title: Eastwind Rest
passages.text:
I am injured, but we can't stop here.

The hozen were... unreliable. The pandaren would be much better allies.

You have seen the refugees in this village, and heard of the yaungol invasion, no?

Well, we've heard from the locals that Eastwind Rest, a nearby village, was destroyed by the Yaungol.

Apparently some survivors have gathered along the road out of town.

Go. Take the road west. Gather the survivors. 

We'll help them rebuild. Then, they will see the advantage of joining the Horde!

passages.title: Eastwind Rest
passages.text: I will not rest until our people are returned and this village rebuilt.

passages.title: Eastwind Rest
passages.text:
Well... we are alive, and that is better than we could have hoped for without your help.

But, if this is truly to become a base of operations for you, and if we are to join your Horde, there is one more thing you must do to guarantee our security.

passages.title: Tummy Trouble
passages.text:
I like Farmer Yoon just dandy as a neighbor, but getting my vote is another matter entirely. He does know that my father is the head of the Union, right?

Anyway, I've got bigger problems to worry about. Lotta folks been getting sick from eating bad vegetables.

Since they bought the produce from my market, my reputation is in jeopardy.

Now I've got an idea to cure the stomach rumbles, but it ain't pretty.

If you'd be willing to... um... hurry things along, I just might be indebted to you.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote II: The Real Culprits
passages.text:
What are YOU doing here, citypaw?

Look, I've got my hands full with a break-in at my shed to the west. Some rascals came in the middle of the night and ransacked the place.

I've got missing seeds, broken tools, and eaten inventory to deal with.

I'll just add it to my list of other troubles: a whole wagon of melons stolen, a broken water pump, animals ruining my harvest...

I wish that I could just get to the bottom of all this already!

passages.title: Haohan's Vote II: The Real Culprits
passages.text: Hmmm, I'm sorry to hear that Haohan's up to his neck in trouble. Thank you for bringing me this news. Maybe we can help him out.

passages.title: Growing the Farm II: Knock on Wood
passages.text:
Sure! I know just the wagon that you're talkin' about!

I can fix it right up, but I'll need wood.

There's a whole lot of it down at the bottom of the lake. If you fish it right out - haha, get it? Fish? Oh I just crack myself up sometimes.

Anyway, you bring me here some 'o that wood and then I'll get right to work!

passages.title: Growing the Farm II: Knock on Wood
passages.text: That lake is plum full o' treasures! You just gotta know what to look for.

passages.title: Growing the Farm II: Knock on Wood
passages.text: Aww yeah, this wood'll do jus' fine. You did good, <name>.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote V: Chief Yip-Yip
passages.text:
You ready for the final step of the plan?

The leader of the Kunzen hozen is a brute by the name of Chief Yip-Yip. It's said that he is nearly impervious to pain.

I've injected the melons with a toxic mixture, so don't try eating them!

Once you get his attention, throw these melons onto the ground. Yip-Yip won't be able to resist a sweet striped melon.

When he takes a bite, he'll be temporarily weakened, and you should find yourself an opening to attack.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote V: Chief Yip-Yip
passages.text: The hozen chief is dead? Our plan worked, <name>!

passages.title: A Second Hand
passages.text:
Despite your best efforts, the work is starting to pile up around here.

Perhaps you could ask one of your best friends if they'd like to help out at Sunsong Ranch.

passages.title: A Second Hand
passages.text: It's a sturdy rake.

passages.title: A Second Hand
passages.text: The talismans on the shrine tinkle softly in the wind.

passages.title: FLAG - Weed War Training
passages.text:
Oh, hello. Are you looking for the owner of this place? Then look to the pandaren up at the top of the stairs. I'm just a visitor... like you.

Now if you'll excuse me, my friends and I trying to decide something. We can talk again afterwards.

passages.title: FLAG - Pest Problems Training
passages.text:
Oh, hello. Are you looking for the owner of this place? Then look to the pandaren up at the top of the stairs. I'm just a visitor... like you.

Now if you'll excuse me, my friends and I trying to decide something. We can talk again afterwards.

passages.title: Blanche's Boomer Brew
passages.text:
Can you smell it in the air? A storm is brewing! And so am I!

Meet me at the hilltop when the storm hits and together we'll whip up a keg of my most famous brew. Can I count on your help?

passages.title: Blanche's Boomer Brew
passages.text:
None too shabby, my <class> friend! We've saved the monastery and still have half a keg left.

Thank you for your help!

passages.title: Helping the Cause
passages.text:
Welcome back, <name>! It seems the Jinyu have taken to our training even better than I had hoped. We're in the final stages of our preparations now.

I need someone to go check in with Amber, Bold Karasshi, and Mishka. See if they need any help to complete their training.

You'll find Karasshi and Mishka here in Pearlfin Village. Amber is training recruits in Slingtail Pits to the northwest.

passages.title: Helping the Cause
passages.text: Is everyone in order and ready to move?

passages.title: Helping the Cause
passages.text: Impressive work, <name>. We should be ready to move out shortly. With our allies at our side, there is no way we can be defeated.

passages.title: Farmhand Freedom
passages.text:
Those Ordo yaungol are working my farmhands to death! It just ain't right.

Please, <class>, save them before it's too late.

passages.title: Farmhand Freedom
passages.text: Look, mister, I don't mean to be telling you your business, but I can still see a lot of my farmhands still out there.

passages.title: Farmhand Freedom
passages.text:
Now ain't you just the thing?

Though, I guess it's not fair to force these here workers to stay with us, now that we don't have much work for 'em...

passages.title: The Late Mrs. Muskpaw
passages.text:
This well worn trinket has several markings on it confessing love and adoration from the late Mrs. Muskpaw.

Perhaps Lao would like his wife's trinket back.

passages.title: The Late Mrs. Muskpaw
passages.text: Oh, and what have you there.

passages.title: The Late Mrs. Muskpaw
passages.text:
Ya never know how much you can lose until you've lost it. My wife passed a few seasons ago, but I can tell you this is a day when I could use her smile the most.

At least she doesn't have to see what these yaungol did to her beloved ranch.

passages.title: Blue Dwarf Needs Food Badly
passages.text:
Oi!

We need ta' get us some food, if we're gonna survive here for long!

Ye' may not know it, but I'm somethin' of a cook me'self. Why don'tcha go out there and fetch us some meaty bits. I can cook 'em up and feed us for weeks! Or, days, at least.

passages.title: Blue Dwarf Needs Food Badly
passages.text: Well... ya' got my meat?

passages.title: Blue Dwarf Needs Food Badly
passages.text: Good work! I'm telliin' ye, these Kun-Lai meaty bits are grade A goodness!

passages.title: Shocking!
passages.text:
Have you ever had a fresh dojani eel <name>? No?

Well you have not lived then! Head north up to the dojani river and fish up a few for us. Be careful, those eels can zap you if you're not careful!

passages.title: Shocking!
passages.text: Were you able to catch the eels?

passages.title: Shocking!
passages.text: These look like some tasty eels <name>!  I'm sure you will love them!

passages.title: Yakity Yak
passages.text:
For now, the yaungol invaders seem content to steal yaks. Surveying the area, however, you notice they could easily move on the Yak Wash at any moment.

Thinning their numbers may help show the yaungol that this area is protected.

passages.title: Yakity Yak
passages.text: Them yak stealing, ranch smashing, bad breath yaungols gotta learn a thing or two about attacking decent folk.

passages.title: Yakity Yak
passages.text:
Well then, I am mighty grateful for you culling some of those yaungols for us.

Hopefully your little display of authority will be enough to discourage them from coming over here.

passages.title: Wrecking the Wreck
passages.text:
To dislodge the alliance ship, we need to find our engineer. He parted ways with us when we were escaping the wreckage.

You should be able to find him somewhere in the western forest. Tell him Korga sent you and he'll get in line to help.

passages.title: Wrecking the Wreck
passages.text:
Korga sent you, eh? Well, I wouldn't mind doing a number on that ship for my own reasons anyway, but it's going to take some work.

Give me a moment to think...

passages.title: Handle With Care
passages.text:
We can help you get your ship free, but we'll need more of the explosives we were trying to take back from the Alliance to make it happen.

I ordered the men to grab all the explosives they could before making our escape. If you sift through the wreckage and bodies to our south, there should be some explosive bundles among them, those that didn't already blow up anyway.

Get me enough of them and I think I can put something together for ya.

passages.title: Handle With Care
passages.text:
You're in one piece. That's a good sign.

Did you get your hands on what I asked for?

passages.title: Handle With Care
passages.text: More than enough. I've got the main control panel constructed. We should be ready very soon!

passages.title: Preying on the Predators
passages.text:
The forest has become far more dangerous ever since Shen-zin Su began shaking. The tigers are agitated and have begun attacking the refugees, and on occasion, me as well.

If these injured and weak survivors are to make it to safety here at the hut, we need to help clear the forest for them.

passages.title: Preying on the Predators
passages.text: Grim work. I've lived in peace with these tigers for as long as I can remember.

passages.title: Preying on the Predators
passages.text: These survivors are in your debt, <class>.

passages.title: Deanimate the Reanimated
passages.text:
The admiral's asked me to take care of a major problem, but my specialty's in healing, not fighting!

The pandaren in the camp here have told me that something is animating the statues to the northeast at Mogujia.

Will you help me out, <name>? We can't afford to have a fight with an army of statues right now.

passages.title: Deanimate the Reanimated
passages.text: Alright! Looks like we won't have a bunch of statues to worry about any more. Good work, <name>!

passages.title: Deanimate the Reanimated
passages.text:
I've got much to do here, <name>. I could use your help.

There's a place to the northwest. The pandaren here call it Mogujia. Something's causing the statues there to animate, and our pandaren friends here are pretty spooked about it.

If they're not dealt with soon, we might have a serious problem. We just moved in. It's not like we can afford to fight a war with an army of statues right now.

passages.title: Deanimate the Reanimated
passages.text: Weren't you going to destroy all of those mogu statues so that we don't, you know, get overrun by them?

passages.title: Deanimate the Reanimated
passages.text: Oh, you dealt with the statues? Good work. Here's something for your trouble.

passages.title: Profiting off of the Past
passages.text:
Let me guess, you're here to deal with the mogu statues that are being reanimated. What a coincidence, I'm here to, um... conduct research on the mogu.

I tell you what, if you bring me as many of the mogu relics in there that you can carry, I'll give you a cut. Of the research... funding.

passages.title: Profiting off of the Past
passages.text: Where am I going to be able to put all of the relics?

passages.title: Profiting off of the Past
passages.text:
Wow! I mean, wow! Thank you, <name>!

Now that you've softened them up, I'm thinking that I might head in. Just a few more relics from around the outskirts. Nothing dangerous.

passages.title: A Zandalari Troll?
passages.text:
While you've been destroying the reanimated mogu statues, the unmistakable accent of a Zandalari troll has been taunting you.

It's clear that the threat to Westerly Rest will not end until he's been dealt with.

passages.title: Instant Courage
passages.text:
It is very bad fortune to travel mountain paths without a good guide. We grummles make the best guides, but many have run away. They fear the mountain pass now. Many good grummles disappear up there.

Grummles are good at many things, but are not very brave. Maybe with fire lotus incense you can make them brave. Then they will show you the way.

passages.title: Instant Courage
passages.text: Did you find the hiding guides?

passages.title: Instant Courage
passages.text: Incense works like a charm! Effects will not last long, so you must hurry!

passages.title: The Rabbitsfoot
passages.text:
The Broketooth hozen stole our Rabbitsfoot! He was the grummle with the biggest luckydo.

This is very bad fortune indeed. Please, <race>, we need our Rabbitsfoot back. We need his good fortune back.

Can you search the Broketooth Outpost for him?

passages.title: The Rabbitsfoot
passages.text:
Look what Broketooths and Knucklethumps did to grummle waystation. Hardly a luckydo to be found.

Grummles had a deal with the hozen. We give them food, and they don't ravage. Whenever they think to ravage, Shado-Pan remind them not to ravage.

But all of Shado-Pan are away defending the wall now. And the hozen want more food than the grummles have.

passages.title: Breaking Broketooth
passages.text:
Hozen only ravage when they think their supplies are too few for their number of mouths.

Problem is, hozen always have more mouths than food.

We have very few grummles these days.

It is a hard thing to ask, but can you be a friend to grummles, and destroy some of the Broketooth hozen south of here? It is the only way to prevent them from destroying the landscape.

passages.title: Breaking Broketooth
passages.text: Thank you, <name>! Hopefully that will slow the Broketooth ravage.

passages.title: Lucky Yakshoe
passages.text:
While you were gone, I saw a group of grummles coming down the Burlap Trail. It was led by my Brother Yakshoe.

But then the Knucklethumps attacked. They took my brother and his grummles north.

Please, adventurer! Save my brother. He always has bad fortune and no luck, but he is my brother. Look for him at the alter in front of Fort Silverback.

passages.title: Lucky Yakshoe
passages.text:
Good fortune for me to be saved by a luckydo like you.

And Brother Rabbitsfoot always say I not have good fortune. Bah!

passages.title: Unleash The Yeti!
passages.text:
Your yeti ride gave me an idea. The Ook of Dook has a pet yeti he named Chomp Chomp.

He uses this yeti to scare other hozen in to making him the leader hozen. We need to get rid of that yeti.

Go to Dooker Dome northwest of here and defeat some of the Cagemasters so Chomp Chomp is not tied up as much.

Yakshoe and I will meet you there with lots of incense and a dirty yak.

passages.title: Unleash The Yeti!
passages.text: We found a yak. Did you take out some hozen?

passages.title: Unleash The Yeti!
passages.text: Ready for the yeti?

passages.title: A Zandalari Troll?
passages.text:
While you've been destroying the reanimated mogu statues, the unmistakable accent of a Zandalari troll has been taunting you.

It's clear that the threat to Westerly Rest will not end until he's been dealt with.

passages.title: The Swarm Begins
passages.text:
Without the wall to protect us, we barely stand a chance. If you hadn't gathered so many people to help us, we wouldn't have a prayer.

Check in with Captain Oakenshield - he should be up near the break in the wall. Kill as many mantid as you can on the way there.

If we win, we win. If we lose, we go down fighting. For Pandaria!

passages.title: The Swarm Begins
passages.text: Look at the SIZE of that thing...

passages.title: The Swarm Begins
passages.text: My wall... I spent my life atop that wall...

passages.title: FLAG - Player Began Finale
passages.text:
Oh, hello. Are you looking for the owner of this place? Then look to the pandaren up at the top of the stairs. I'm just a visitor... like you.

Now if you'll excuse me, my friends and I trying to decide something. We can talk again afterwards.

passages.title: Out with the Scouts
passages.text:
We'd been briefed on mogu sightings in the Vale, but the situation is worse than we had anticipated.

Scouts are swarming all over the ruins to the northwest, gathering intel and stealing treasures.

Your objective is clear - dispatch of any scouts you see. An army cannot move if we take out its eyes.

passages.title: Out with the Scouts
passages.text: Well done, <race>. That should send a clear message to the mogu - we are not to be trifled with.

passages.title: Killing the Quilen
passages.text:
We've taken care of the scout problem for now, but there are still advance mogu forces inside the Guo-Lai Halls down the hill.

Unfortunately, their vicious guard dogs are protecting their operations deeper in the ruins.

Go and dispatch of their beasts. Be on your guard - they can be quite good at blending into their surroundings.

passages.title: Killing the Quilen
passages.text: Good. Those dogs know no mercy, so it's good that you showed them none.

passages.title: Stones of Power
passages.text:
Many thousands of years ago, the rulers of the Vale sought energy from a powerful crystal known as Revelite.

With this substance, they were able to power cities, factories, and engines of war.

Zhi the Harmonious has asked us to collect some crystals and bring them back to the city.

Keep an eye out for them while you are in the ruins.

passages.title: Stones of Power
passages.text: Did you find the crystals?

passages.title: Stones of Power
passages.text:
Mmmhmm. These will do nicely.

I'll have them sent back to camp immediately.

passages.title: The Guo-Lai Halls
passages.text:
As you pass by the great door, you hear sounds from deep inside.

Anji mentioned that advance mogu scouts had been sighted in this area. Perhaps they made their way down to the depths below.

Your senses tingling, you decide to investigate.

passages.title: The Guo-Lai Halls
passages.text:
Your instincts were correct, <name>.

In ancient times, the Guo-Lai Halls were home to powerful treasures.

We must do everything we can to stop this mogu warlord from accessing those sealed crypts.

passages.title: Battle Spear of the Thunder King
passages.text:
I have received some troubling news, <name>.

The mogu are plotting to steal three artifacts of power from the Vale.

We must retrieve the artifacts immediately and hide them for safekeeping.

The first artifact is the Battle Spear of the Thunder King.

Upon emperor Lei Shen's death, the spear was placed in an ancient shrine to the northwest.

Bring the spear back to me.

passages.title: Battle Spear of the Thunder King
passages.text:
It was said that the most powerful of ancient mogu could call the powers of the elements.

The Thunder King himself could channel the forces of lightning onto his spear.

passages.title: Battle Spear of the Thunder King
passages.text:
Well done, <name>, although it pains me to lay my eyes upon that wretched spear.

This foul weapon murdered thousands of innocents.

As long as I live, the mogu shall never have possession of it again.

passages.title: Battle Helm of the Thunder King
passages.text:
The second artifact of power is the Battle Helm of the Thunder King.

Emperor Lei Shen wore the helm into every battle. It became so well-known that his enemies would flee at the mere sight of it.

When the Emperor died, they placed the helm in the very bottom of the Guo-Lai Halls to the west, surrounded by thousands of terracotta soldiers.

Thus, they could look upon their leader and follow him into death.

passages.title: Battle Helm of the Thunder King
passages.text: History claims that Lei Shen feared no enemy except for one. And in the end, it was death that finally defeated him.

passages.title: Battle Helm of the Thunder King
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

While our soldiers fight the mogu on the battlefield, I work to strip away the power of their legends.

In time, Lei Shen shall be no more than the shadow of a memory.

passages.title: Battle Axe of the Thunder King
passages.text:
The final artifact is the Thunder King's axe.

Lei Shen charged into battle with his spear in one hand, and his axe in the other.

It is said that he could throw his axe with brutal accuracy, and when it hit its target, it made a sound like crashing thunder.

After his death, the axe was placed in a ceremonial chamber to the southwest.

Needless to say, we must not let it fall into the mogu's hands.

passages.title: Battle Axe of the Thunder King
passages.text: Did you find the axe?

passages.title: Battle Axe of the Thunder King
passages.text: Such modesty, <name>. I witnessed what you did to retrieve the axe. Well done.

passages.title: The Final Power
passages.text:
I never thought it would come to this!

Leven went to face Warlord Zhao-Jin the Bloodletter at the top of the palace steps, but our reinforcements cannot get through!

We are the only ones who stand between him and the Vale's greatest... and most deadly... powers.

Please, <name>, you must find a way to stop him!

passages.title: The Final Power
passages.text:
What you have accomplished today will live on in stories for ages to come.

With your help, we have saved the Vale from a terrible enemy.

Today, we dealt a painful blow to the mogu. They will never stop their attempts to seize the Vale, but it will be a long time before they try a full scale attack again.

passages.title: Moving On
passages.text:
Your journey in this land has already proven most eventful, traveler. And mine, it appears, is destined to continue for a time.

A chain of events began when your people arrived here, and while some of those happenings are traumatic to behold, I feel there must be a larger purpose behind your presence.

For now it is wisest that you leave this place and explore Pandaria's other regions.

Speak to me when you are ready to leave.

passages.title: Moving On
passages.text:
Be wise, traveler.

Prove to these inhabitants that there is more to your people than war and destruction.

passages.title: Pandaren Prisoners
passages.text:
Look, I know the Alliance needs recruits, and there's just not enough of us here right now to make a fighting presence of this town.

But I know that the yaungol over at Fire Camp Ordo, to the northwest, have taken many of my people as prisoners. And I also know that if you would be willing to rescue them from their captivity, they'd more than likely be willing to join the Alliance.

What do you say, <name>?

passages.title: Pandaren Prisoners
passages.text:
Well, if it isn't our hero, <name>.

I really wasn't sure we stood a fighting chance out here, you know?

These guys may be a little rough around the edges, but we'll be able to whip 'em into shape. And when we do, we'll have a real fighting chance at holding our own here in Kun-Lai.

Good work.

passages.title: In Tents Channeling
passages.text:
The yaungol of Fire Camp Ordo are a dire threat. I need you to head northwest and take out their leader.

Unfortunately, his four subordinates are maintaining a fire barrier that prevents us from getting to him in the adjoining cave.

Take them out and the shield will come down. You'll find them in their tents, channeling.

passages.title: The Guo-Lai Halls
passages.text:
The mogu are up to something, I can feel it.

They've been sending scouts down into the Guo-Lai Halls.

According to the caretakers, the Halls are home to ancient treasures of emperors past. Not only riches, but artifacts of great power.

We must prevent the mogu from accessing these treasures! Go down the ramp to the northwest and stop them!

passages.title: The Guo-Lai Halls
passages.text:
It looks like you may have averted a great disaster, <name>.

If this mogu warlord seeks the treasures of the Guo-Lai Halls, we must do all that we can to stop him.

passages.title: Pandaren Prisoners
passages.text:
Look, I know the Horde needs recruits, and there's just not enough of us here right now to make a fighting presence of this town.

But I know that the yaungol over at Fire Camp Ordo, to the west, have taken many of my people as prisoners. And I also know that if you would be willing to rescue them from their captivity, they'd more than likely be willing to join the Horde.

What do you say, <name>?

passages.title: Pandaren Prisoners
passages.text:
Well, it looks like we've got ourselves a little army, here, thanks to you.

They may not look like much yet, but a little Horde discipline and we'll have them in fighting shape in no time.

By the way, <name>... good work.

passages.title: In Tents Channeling
passages.text:
The yaungol of Fire Camp Ordo are the worst threat we're facing. I need you to head west and take out their leader.

The coward is hiding in a cave, which is protected by a fire shield cast by his four underlings.

Take them out and the shield will come down. You'll find them in their tents, channeling.

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
You've taken the shield down at Fire Camp Ordo. Go back there before the shield goes up again.

Time to head into the cave and slay their chief!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text: <name>, what are you doing here? The Ordo Warbringer isn't dead yet!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
You've done it, <name>! I'm in your debt!

Again!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
You've taken the shield down at Fire Camp Ordo. Get back over there before they get that shield up again.

Slay the Warbringer of the Ordo!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
Once again you've accomplished what no one else could.

Was there any doubt?

passages.title: The Defense of Shado-Pan Fallback
passages.text:
I sent for reinforcements from the Shado-Pan Monastery, but have heard nothing back. We have already lost the town.

A few lucky villagers may have survived, but we are pinned down here.

We do not have time to entertain strangers. If you can fight, help my men defend this tower. If not, leave, for you will not survive long here.

passages.title: The Defense of Shado-Pan Fallback
passages.text: Have you dealt with the yaungol yet?

passages.title: The Defense of Shado-Pan Fallback
passages.text: You have bought us some time to breathe. We must not despair - instead, we must act.

passages.title: Sudden, Unexpected Crocolisk Aggression
passages.text:
Normally, my day consists of catching fish, and then eating the fish I caught, followed by sleeping. Note that I did not include "fight with a crocolisk" in that list of activities.

You look like a handy <class>. Can you go get rid of some of these crocolisks, so I can get back to my regular routine? The crocolisks normally keep to themselves up at Kea Krak, to the northwest.

passages.title: Sudden, Unexpected Crocolisk Aggression
passages.text: What would make the crocs attack like this?

passages.title: Sudden, Unexpected Crocolisk Aggression
passages.text:
Yesterday, we were fishing happily. Today, the crocs just started... tryin' to eat us.

Strange.

passages.title: Turnabout
passages.text:
Our true enemies are the sha, not the yaungol.

The sha are emotion manifest. Destructive, yes. But undisciplined. Undisciplined force cannot last. The flood, in dispersion, loses its force. The wildfire burns its fuel.

And, discipline and wisdom can turn their destructive energy against themselves.

Bring me the essences of the sha in the village, and I will explain further.

passages.title: Turnabout
passages.text: Have you harvested their essences?

passages.title: Turnabout
passages.text:
Good. Now you will see how to defeat unbridled rage.

I will craft these into a trap for Kobai, the leader of the yaungol. Though he will be snared, and we will defeat him, he is not our ultimate target...

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text:
Thank the heavenly spirits for you, <class>! I don't know how much longer I could've lasted.

There are other Firebough Nook survivors, I'm sure of it. Will you help rescue them and get us to the safety of Shado-Pan Fallback?

passages.title: Balance Without Violence
passages.text: Some of the fish that the Unga hozen have gathered don't seem do be dead yet. There may still be time to throw them back into the water.

passages.title: Buried Hozen Treasure
passages.text:
The map you hold is crinkled, dirty, and poorly drawn, but you can see a big X on a beach.

Is there buried treasure somewhere on this island?

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text:
Oh thank you, thank you, thank you. If you hadn't come along...

Wait! There must be other survivors in the Nook like me!

Please, <class>, I beg you. Rescue the rest of my citizens and deliver us safely to Shado-Pan Fallback.

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text:
Oh, thank you! There's no way I could have made it back on my own.

Come to think of it, there must be others around Firebough Nook that need to be rescued. Shall we go collect them and then head to the safety of Shado-Pan Fallback?

passages.title: Misery
passages.text:
While you are in the water below, you should slay Nahassa, the mortbreath patriarch. He suffers. I can feel his death cries ululating up to the surface of the lagoon.

Find his cave, and put him out of his misery. Not because it will solve Marista's crocolisk problem. Simply out of mercy.

passages.title: Misery
passages.text: Please, <name>. Even the great beasts of this world have a right to die in dignity.

passages.title: Misery
passages.text: Nahassa's fevered suffering has come to an end.

passages.title: To Winter's Blossom
passages.text:
The battle against the Sha is eternal - we can not leave this place. 

But I am troubled by the absence of reinforcements from the Monastery given that we sent for them days ago. 

You have performed admirably, perhaps you could travel to Winter's Blossom, our base camp on the way to the Shado-Pan Monastery. Speak with Lin Silentstrike once you arrive - he should know what is happening. To get there, travel north of the village and follow the road through Shado-Li Basin to Winter's Blossom.

passages.title: To Winter's Blossom
passages.text:
Shado-Master Chong sent you, hmm?

Yes, we received his request for reinforcements.

We are in no position to grant it, however. We've just concluded a battle of our own, and the monastery's been locked up tight. 

We can't even get reinforcements here, and we're just down the hill!

passages.title: Provoking the Trolls
passages.text:
We've managed to push them back this far, but I doubt that we will remain safe for long if we do not deal with them once and for all.

My husband, coward or fool that he is, does not wish to provoke them. I will not be cowed so.

We will do just that. Slay their forward scouts. Perhaps we can provoke - and then defeat - their leader.

passages.title: Destroy the Leaders
passages.text:
And, now they fear you.

Their leaders, a Blademaster and a Mage, lie deeper in the ruins. Kill them.
Make them hurt. For us.

passages.title: Chasing Hope
passages.text:
Chi-Ji is always with us. Even when he is not here in the Cradle, pieces of his spirit run through the forests and beaches of the island, watching us and testing us.

Prove your dexterity in the eyes of Chi-Ji, <name>. Find and catch the spirits of the crane.

passages.title: Chasing Hope
passages.text: Return when you are finished, <name>. Now go!

passages.title: Chasing Hope
passages.text: Chi-Ji smiles on you.

passages.title: Students of Chi-Ji
passages.text:
Our order prides itself on excellence in combat. We hone these combat skills by dueling one another, here on the Cradle of Chi-Ji.

Prove yourself in the eyes of the Red Crane. Venture south, into the center of the island, and duel with your fellow students.

passages.title: Students of Chi-Ji
passages.text: Your trial is not yet complete, <name>.

passages.title: Students of Chi-Ji
passages.text: With every battle - a win or a loss - you improve. You become faster, hardier, cleverer... better.

passages.title: Honor, Even in Death
passages.text:
Hmm... If Shado-Master Chong trusted you, perhaps you can help us.

The yaungol are our enemies.

Still, we must prove we are better than they. We will show them honor in death.

As after most battles, the carrion birds have begun gathering. Thin their numbers, so the bodies of our foes will not be desecrated. They've gathered at the battlefield to the west.

passages.title: Honor, Even in Death
passages.text: Killing those birds may not soothe my anger, but at least it proves that we are better than our enemies. They would not do such a thing.

passages.title: Honor, Even in Death
passages.text: Good. After what they have done, I would not show the Yaungol kindness in life. But neither will I allow their bodies to be eaten by the birds.

passages.title: Minh Do-Tan
passages.text:
Your next challenger is another relatively new trainee. His name is Minh Do-Tan, and he has won his last two matches.

He will be waiting for you near the crane statue to the south.

passages.title: Minh Do-Tan
passages.text: Fight hard, <name>.

passages.title: Minh Do-Tan
passages.text: Well done, <name>. You are beginning to make a name for yourself.

passages.title: Julia Bates
passages.text:
We welcome all kinds here within the Cradle, as long as they recognize and subscribe to the ideologies of the Red Crane. One of our new, more exotic trainees comes from the human kingdoms to the northeast. She goes by the rather foreign-sounding name of Julia Bates.

She is your next challenger. You will find her on the island's western shore.

passages.title: Julia Bates
passages.text: Another fight handily won. I anxiously await your next match, <name>.

passages.title: Dextrous Izissha
passages.text:
Jinyu normally avoid our order, but every few years, we find one that subscribes to the way of the Crane. One such jinyu is Dextrous Izissha.

Izissha is your next challenger. He waits for you on the island's southwestern shore.

passages.title: Dextrous Izissha
passages.text:
Excellent work, <name>! You continue to gain favor in the eyes of Chi-Ji.

Your next battle will be one to remember. You will not be fighting a trainee. Instead, you will face one of your trainers.

passages.title: Kuo-Na Quillpaw
passages.text:
Most of the duels within the Cradle take place between two trainees. Rarely, when a trainee exhibits a rare amount of skill, they will have an opportunity to duel their trainer.

Today, you duel against Kuo-Na. She will be waiting for you at the Pedestal of Hope.

passages.title: Kuo-Na Quillpaw
passages.text:
You continue to impress, <name>.

Come again soon. Your training is not over yet.

passages.title: Ellia Ravenmane: Revenge
passages.text:
Your "rival" has appeared again. Ellia Ravenmane has been avoiding her duties on the island, instead focusing on personal training, with the intent to defeat you in battle.

"I will destroy <name>," she said.

I have honored her request for a rematch, but I will be keeping a close eye on her. Her motives may be shifting in a dangerous direction.

passages.title: Ellia Ravenmane: Revenge
passages.text: I will consult directly with Chi-Ji about Ellia's behavior. She treads on thin ice.

passages.title: Tukka-Tuk
passages.text:
You are making a name for yourself, <name>. I received a challenge from one of our more skilled competitors. He believes you are not as strong as you seem.

His name is Tukka-Tuk, the hozen. If you've ever fought against hozen before, you know that their apparent juvenility belies their battle acumen. Good luck.

passages.title: Tukka-Tuk
passages.text:
Well done, as usual.

I trust I will see you again soon.

passages.title: Huck Wheelbarrow
passages.text:
Usually our trainees are adventurers like yourself, or monks from Tian Monastery, or occasionally retired Shado-Pan. Very rarely, though, we will greet trainees that have no fighting experience whatsoever.

Huck Wheelbarrow is one such trainee. He has requested a duel with you. Look for him on the island's western shore.

passages.title: Huck Wheelbarrow
passages.text:
There remains only one trainee ranked higher than you.

I have a feeling that you will be facing him when you return.

passages.title: Mindel Sunspeaker
passages.text:
Our highest-ranked trainee is an outsider like you. It is both strange and exciting to live in a time when so many foreigners have embraced the way of the Crane.

Your challenger's name is Mindel Sunspeaker, and he awaits you within Angkhal Pavilion.

passages.title: Mindel Sunspeaker
passages.text:
You are now our highest-ranked trainee. You are no longer obligated to participate in trainee duels. Congratulations!

Of course, there are still other ways to prove yourself. I have the feeling I will be seeing you again...

passages.title: Yan Quillpaw
passages.text:
You have already defeated Kuo-Na Quillpaw. You have not yet fought her brother, Yan.

He will meet you at the Pedestal of Hope, and he will not hold back. His reputation as a trainer is at stake.

passages.title: Yan Quillpaw
passages.text:
And with that victory, I suppose we've run out of challengers for you to fight! Other than me, of course.

But... I don't fight. I mean, you wouldn't want to fight me. It would... not go well for you.

passages.title: Fat Long-Fat: Rematch
passages.text:
Fat Long-Fat has requested another match with you. I find this strange. And concerning.

He will be waiting atop the Dome Belrissa.

passages.title: Fat Long-Fat: Rematch
passages.text:
I believe I understand why he wanted to fight you a second time, though I need to speak with Chi-Ji before I can be sure.

Come back soon, <name>. I think it is time you learned the true nature of Fat Long-Fat.

passages.title: Thelonius
passages.text:
When we last spoke, I promised to tell you the secret of Fat Long-Fat. I still plan to tell you that secret... after I determine your worth.

I will meet you on the western shore, and we will duel.

passages.title: Thelonius
passages.text:
You are truly worthy of the secret of Fat Long-Fat. Here it is:

Fat Long-Fat and Chi-Ji are one and the same. Fat Long-Fat is the Red Crane.

He believes that the Cradle is in great danger.

He believes there is one person that can save it.

He believes that you are that person, <name>.

Stay in touch.

passages.title: Champion of Chi-Ji
passages.text:
While you will always hold a place of honor among our order, you are still welcome to participate in our duels.

One of our current champions awaits you in the Dome Balrissa. I know that they would be honored to duel with you.

passages.title: Champion of Chi-Ji
passages.text:
Done masterfully, as always.

We hope to see you again soon, <name>.

passages.title: Shut it Down
passages.text:
I mussed up. Bad.

It's hard work cutting seeds out of kafa berries! But I noticed goots eat the berries up and give back the seeds... in a day or so.

I fed everything I had to the goots on Kota Peak and now they're nuts! Chargin' everything that moves.

Kota used to be safe for Grummles to gather kafa. Not anymore. Not with them goots. Will you help?

passages.title: Shut it Down
passages.text: Thank you, friend. Let this be a lesson to you: never feed the goots.

passages.title: Gourmet Kafa
passages.text:
It was genius: kafa berries go in the goot, seeds come out.

Kafa'kota is already rare and worth a fortune, but my invention--Kafa'goot--is GOURMET.

But it's over now. Uncle is upset and peak is a muss. All that's left is to collect the rest of the Kafa'goot and never make it again.

I won't ask you to gather it--kind of a mussy task, not fit for hero-- just mark it so I can find it easily when the mountain is safe again.

passages.title: Gourmet Kafa
passages.text:
Great, I'll get up there and... harvest them soon.

<Cousin Gootfur begins wrapping long strips of linen around his hands.>

Can't believe I thought this was a good idea.

passages.title: Off the Wall!
passages.text:
The yaungol on the wall here are providing covering fire for the ones below. I don't know what Lao-chen is thinking, but I want you to deal with these archers.

The good news is, up here we've got the spirit of the Ox helping us. When they're weakened, the ox spirit will stun them and you can use it to knock 'em off the wall.

You'll find the archers just out that door.

passages.title: Off the Wall!
passages.text: Come on, come on.

passages.title: Off the Wall!
passages.text: Ha! I could see them flying. Good work.

passages.title: A Terrible Sacrifice
passages.text:
I have an idea, and... am prepared to make a terrible sacrifice.

As much as I know that we need my stout brew, to fortify our defenders for the long-term security of the Ox Gate...

It is too painful to discuss details now, but please - while you are up here defending the wall, gather the barrels of oil they are using to light their arrows. We will need them.

passages.title: A Terrible Sacrifice
passages.text: Do you have the oil?

passages.title: A Terrible Sacrifice
passages.text: Alright. I am off to prepare our next move. Good luck, friend.

passages.title: Jumping the Shark
passages.text:
There is only one way to kill sharks where I come from, with your bare hands!

I dumped a good amount of chum in the water just off the dock here, this place should be crawling with the local reef sharks in no time. Hop on the first one you see and take it out!

passages.title: Jumping the Shark
passages.text: Did you show that shark who's boss?

passages.title: Jumping the Shark
passages.text: That was a huge shark you took out <name>!  Color me impressed!

passages.title: Bright Bait
passages.text:
Certain fish are only attracted to bright lights. The forest north of here is home to a local pandaren firefly called a suncrawler.

You should be able to find them on the base of the tree trunks all around that area. Bring me back a handful of them and I can use them for bait!

passages.title: Bright Bait
passages.text: Any luck with those suncrawlers?

passages.title: Bright Bait
passages.text: These should do nicely <name>.  Thanks for the help!

passages.title: Sotelo's Quest
passages.text:
Push the plunger.

PUSH IT!

passages.title: Piranha!
passages.text:
Certain fish are very difficult to catch. The wolf piranha falls squarely into this category.

Lucky for me that you showed up! Put those fishing skills to the test and bring me back a few from the krasarang river due northwest of here.

passages.title: Piranha!
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: Piranha!
passages.text: I see you still have all your fingers, nice work.

passages.title: Regaining Honor
passages.text:
<name>, the yaungol warchief, Humongous, killed Shado-Master Zhen. He has his banner.

You have to kill Humongous and regain Zhen's honor! If you don't, I will.

passages.title: Profiting off of the Past
passages.text:
<A relic drops off of the statue. Hmm, these could prove to be valuable to the right person.>

<There's a collector on the outskirts of the ruins. Perhaps he'd be interested in purchasing them from you?>

passages.title: Risking It All
passages.text:
Wait, what?! How could he be so reckless? Blowing the ship free is insane! They could kill Shen-zin Su, and all of us with it. 

I know we don't have much time, but we need to think of another way...

passages.title: Risking It All
passages.text: The first step is done, but now we must save Shen-zin Su!

passages.title: First Assault
passages.text:
Now that we have had time to assess our enemies' weaknesses, it is time for us to deal the yaungol a direct blow.

Go and confront the Osul Sharphorn up the mesa to the west.

Let them know that we are here, and that we are not scared of their threats.

passages.title: First Assault
passages.text: Well done, <name>. I hope you showed those cretins no mercy.

passages.title: Running Rampant
passages.text:
There is one thing that every army needs, and that is a supply line.

The enemy camp to the west contains a large beast herd, which serves as the yaungol army's main source of food.

Luckily for us, the yaks and mushan beasts of this region are easily scared.

Sneak in, give the beasts a good slap, and watch the results.

passages.title: Running Rampant
passages.text:
Ohohoho! I saw those animals trailing dust from up here.

Those yaungol are probably still wondering what happened.

passages.title: Seeing Red
passages.text:
Ahead of us is the main thrust of the yaungol army.

Here, they prepare their vast army to attack the villages of Kun-Lai.

If we strike at the Osul now, we can cut them at their very core.

Remember, for every of their number that we strike down here, we save one of our own back at home.

passages.title: Seeing Red
passages.text:
That should put a serious dent in their numbers.

I doubt they will be able to recover from such losses.

passages.title: Pitching In
passages.text:
The yaungol's siege weapons - those ballista spearthrowers down there - are tearing apart our defenses both at Longying Oupost and in Kun-Lai Summit.

Those terrible weapons must be destroyed.

Take these explosives. I've covered them in the pitch that you collected.

Toss them at those ballistas, and we'll give the yaungol a little taste of their own medicine.

passages.title: Pitching In
passages.text: Fire is a cruel weapon. Luckily, we are only using it to destroy weapons of war.

passages.title: Pitching In
passages.text:
Good, <class>.

Now that they cannot hide behind their siege weapons, they have no choice but to face us.

passages.title: The Exile
passages.text:
What is there to say, stranger?

I fought Jung Duk and lost. I was the fool to believe he would fight fairly.

Now, my own brothers turned against me, and here I am, speaking to our enemies.

I know you have come for Osul blood.

I only ask that you hunt down the three who betrayed me.

Urang, who poisoned my drink. Ku-Tong, who bent my spear. And Battat, whose dagger slipped into my side as my victory was assured.

Do this, and I can die in peace.

passages.title: The Exile
passages.text:
How could they have betrayed me? They were once my brothers!

Why did they turn on me? WHY?

I hate them! I will slaughter them all!

passages.title: The Exile
passages.text:
It pleases me to know those cowards died at your hands.

Perhaps now, this burning tide in my heart will ebb.

passages.title: In Search of Suna
passages.text:
I have bad news. When I returned, Suna was already gone.

The others say that she took her things and headed down the road to the east, muttering about hunting down the source of the yaungol aggression.

I cannot allow her to venture into dangerous territory alone.

I've already prepared a group of soldiers to push further east.

We are leaving shortly. Hop on the caravan if you wish to travel with the Shado-Pan. You can also meet us there if you wish.

passages.title: In Search of Suna
passages.text: Well, we made it.

passages.title: Dust to Dust
passages.text:
If we are to make camp here, we cannot leave all of these yaungol bodies lying to rot.

Take this torch and set fire to the villagers' corpses.

The incense from the torch should purify the earth and air around them as well.

Even our enemies deserve to be laid to rest.

passages.title: Dust to Dust
passages.text: The stench of death is overpowering.

passages.title: Dust to Dust
passages.text:
Good work, <name>.

Hopefully, their spirits are in a better place.

passages.title: Slaying the Scavengers
passages.text:
The rotting corpses are attracting hyena scavengers.

In addition to spreading diseases from feeding on the dead, the feral creatures will attack us on sight.

Go and eradicate the beasts. It is unfortunate, but ultimately for the best.

passages.title: Slaying the Scavengers
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. It was an unpleasant task, but it had to be done.

passages.title: Totemic Research
passages.text:
As we entered the village, I couldn't help but notice yaungol totems lying around this camp.

I have a suspicion that there are dark forces at work here, and those totems may be the key to drawing them out.

Could you bring me some of these totems for further inspection? I would like to study them.

passages.title: Totemic Research
passages.text: I do believe the totems could be of use to us.

passages.title: Totemic Research
passages.text:
I was right! These totems were once used to store and conduct immense magical energies.

I do believe I can use them once again to do the same.

passages.title: Last Toll of the Yaungol
passages.text:
Ban has asked me to explore the village to determine what happened here.

I noticed smoke rising up from the east, the west, northwest, and the south.

I need someone I trust to watch my back.

What do you say? Want to help me on my first scouting mission?

passages.title: Last Toll of the Yaungol
passages.text: Something terrible must have happened here.

passages.title: Last Toll of the Yaungol
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, <name>.

We cannot know exactly what happened here, but it's clear that something caused the yaungol to turn on one another.

What kind of power could do this?

passages.title: Spiteful Spirits
passages.text:
The spirits of the fallen villagers have risen! I can feel the hatred emanating from the spirits.

<name>, if we are to survive here, we must defend ourselves. This is the only way we can put them to rest.

passages.title: Spiteful Spirits
passages.text: The air is thick with their malicious intent.

passages.title: Spiteful Spirits
passages.text: Well done. We cannot bring them retribution, but at least we can end their rage.

passages.title: The Point of No Return
passages.text:
One of our rangers reported seeing Suna up the hill to the northwest.

I am relieved to find her safe. I had feared what she would do in her grief.

Would you go speak to her on my behalf?

Take this totem with you. If you encounter any danger along the way, you may find it useful.

passages.title: The Point of No Return
passages.text:
If I could change the past, I would. If I could take Lin's place, I would.

In a thousand lifetimes, I will never be able to repay Suna's loss, or share even a measure of her grief.

passages.title: The Point of No Return
passages.text:
What? She was possessed by the Sha of Hatred?

No. NO!

Despite our differences, she was one of us. Today, the Shado-Pan has lost a dear sister.

Her death will not be in vain. I will not rest until I have defeated the Sha of Hatred!

Suna, I swear this to you!

passages.title: A Spear Through My Side, A Chain Through My Soul
passages.text:
My fate is sealed. The yaungol put this spear in my side. The wound will kill me.

The yaungol hold me in place with their twisted, corrupted magic. The indignity of it hurts worse than my spear-wound.

My death, I cannot stop. My imprisonment... you may be able to help me with this.

passages.title: A Spear Through My Side, A Chain Through My Soul
passages.text: I will not die before having my revenge.

passages.title: A Spear Through My Side, A Chain Through My Soul
passages.text:
I am freed.

The yaungol must be stopped.

passages.title: Emergency Care
passages.text:
I... am alive... but barely. They killed the rest. My friends... and family...

I must return to the village... But, I do not have long, and cannot move on my own... are you a healer? I... have a healing potion in my hut... search my belongings. You can use your magic, if you have it.

passages.title: Emergency Care
passages.text: Thank you. I suppose... I'll need to ask you to do a bit more before I can return to the village. I cannot leave the bodies of my friends and family here.

passages.title: Staying Connected
passages.text:
The Tongue of Ba-Shon should allow us to communicate from long distances, <name>.

If the relic works the way I think it will, I should be able to stay here and continue my meditations while you do some scouting in the Valley of Emperors.

Mishi will take you to the edge of the valley so that we can test my theory. I would hate for you to be in the tombs with no way to contact me. That would be horrible!

passages.title: Staying Connected
passages.text:
Very good! The relic works!

It appears there is more going on in the Valley of Emperors than I had anticipated. It is crucial we figure out why the Mogu are opening the tombs.

passages.title: An End to Everything
passages.text:
These spirits must have been released when the tombs were opened... 

Death was not final for the Mogu. Instead, death was merely a stop over on the path to a new body. Spiritbinders used a foul magic to transfer spirits from one shell to the next.

Years of being trapped in the tombs has left them confused. They need to be destroyed before their confusion turns to anger or worse, they find a new shell.

passages.title: An End to Everything
passages.text: Have you disposed of the spirits yet?

passages.title: An End to Everything
passages.text:
You have done them a great service, <name>.

It is a cruel fate to be stuck between the living world and the afterlife.

passages.title: Breaking the Emperor's Shield
passages.text:
The Mogu have been scattered and sparse in number for many years. Their purpose in the valley makes sense now.

With this many restless spirits they can build themselves an army using the guardians buried in each tomb. Combined with the Zandalari forces this would be devastating!

The Tomb of Secrets houses elite warriors called the Emperor's Shield. They must not be resurrected! You'll find the tomb on the highest rise to the southwest.

passages.title: Breaking the Emperor's Shield
passages.text: Have you gone to the Tomb of Secrets yet?

passages.title: Breaking the Emperor's Shield
passages.text:
The Mogu and the Zandalari intend to resurrect the Thunder King?!

We cannot let this happen, <name>! The Thunder King will rain destruction on this land with his return.

passages.title: Lessons from History
passages.text:
The Thunder King was a vicious Emperor and with the Zandalari at his side he was unstoppable. His return would surely return this land to turmoil and misery.

You must locate his remains and take them somewhere safe. The Tablet of Thunder should help you figure out how to access his tomb.

passages.title: Lessons from History
passages.text: Have you read the tablet?

passages.title: Lessons from History
passages.text: They will need to move the remains to a secure location. We must go after them!

passages.title: Justice
passages.text:
After the mercenaries robbed us, most left.

But one of them... after the others took all we had, he ran the rest of us through. For sport!

Get justice for the fallen. Perhaps news of their death will raise my spirits enough to go on.

You'll find them just west of here.

passages.title: Justice
passages.text: Ahh.. they are dead. Already, I can feel my spirits lifting. Soon I will have the strength to return to the village.

passages.title: By the Falls, For the Fallen
passages.text:
I do not wish to dishonor my friends and leave them in unmarked graves.

Yet, we have never needed to bury so many at once, and I am in no condition to gather materials.

Please, visit the lakes that hug the mountains edge along the road to the south. Underneath the waterfalls there, you will find stones that have been polished to a sheen by the falling water. They will make suitable headstones.

passages.title: By the Falls, For the Fallen
passages.text: The stones - have you brought them?

passages.title: By the Falls, For the Fallen
passages.text: Good. Thank you. After this, I cannot imagine leaving my fellows to less than a proper burial.

passages.title: A Foot in the Door
passages.text:
<Lord Taran immediately pins you down with his steely gaze.>

<class>, you bear the marks of many a past battle.

Good! We need more seasoned people like you to hold back the front.

We've managed to secure a foothold here, but the yaungol are desperate to remove our presence.

If you wish to prove your worth, go down the hill and show the yaungol that we will not back down.

passages.title: A Foot in the Door
passages.text: We are slowly gaining ground.

passages.title: A Foot in the Door
passages.text:
Good. I can see that you are capable.

I hope to rely on your talents for what is to come.

passages.title: Checking In
passages.text: When the trolls came, they brought their mercenary... friends with them. I saw them go past us, to the fishing camp in the northwest. My cousin, a healer, lives there - can you check in with him and make sure he and his village are well?

passages.title: Checking In
passages.text: Ahh... My cousin is wise to be worried... I am not well...

passages.title: Preparing the Remains
passages.text:
Thank you much, friend. After this tragedy, it is good that fortune has smiled on us and sent you.

You have gotten justice for my fallen friends, and gathered the necessary materials to honor them. I will gather their bodies, prepare the materials for their funerals, and meet you at the graveyard. 

In the meantime, however, please return to my cousin and ask him to gather the villagers for the funeral.

passages.title: Preparing the Remains
passages.text: I see... it is tragic what has happened there. We will meet you at the graveyard to honor them.

passages.title: Shut it Down
passages.text:
My cousin over at Kota Basecamp mussed up. He mussed up bad.

He was too lazy to cut seeds out of kafa berries by hand, but he noticed goots eat the berries up and give back the seeds... in a day or so.

He fed everything he had to the goots on Kota Peak and now they're nuts! Chargin' everything that moves.

Kota used to be safe for Grummles to gather kafa. Not anymore. Not with them goots. Will you help?

passages.title: Shut it Down
passages.text: Thank you for helping to correct my mistake, friend. Let this be a lesson to you: never feed the goots.

passages.title: Gourmet Kafa
passages.text:
It was a crazy idea: kafa berries go in the goot, seeds come out.

Kafa'kota is already rare and worth a fortune, but my cousin's invention--Kafa'goot--is GOURMET.

But it's over now. Uncle Keenbean is upset and peak is a muss. All that's left is to collect the rest of the Kafa'goot and never make it again.

I won't ask you to gather it--kind of a mussy task, not fit for hero-- just mark it so we can find it easily when the mountain is safe again.

passages.title: Gourmet Kafa
passages.text:
I'd heard an adventurer was up there marking the deposits. Mussy work for someone with your skills, but I appreciate it.

I'll get up there and... harvest them soon.

<Cousin Gootfur begins wrapping long strips of linen around his hands.>

Can't believe I thought this was a good idea.

passages.title: Trouble Brewing
passages.text:
Lots of yetis in Kota, yup. Usually not too dangerous. Usually just eat goots.

Then stupid Cousin Gootfur over at Kota Basecamp fed kafa to the goots, and the yeti ate them goots.

Now they're moody, cranky, sleep a lot but never seem rested. Typical kafa addicts.

Gonna come outta those caves soon, I'm sure. Come lookin' for more kafa.

Then we all in trouble.

passages.title: Trouble Brewing
passages.text:
Ah, hello there! Tallmug sent a messenger yak over explaining that you would be helping us with our yeti problems.

And you weren't torn to shreds! Yeti's are tough enough on their own - can't imagine what a cranky kafa-addict yeti must be like. You're brave. Or lucky. Or dumb.

Maybe all three.

passages.title: The Tongue of Ba-Shon
passages.text:
Thank you for coming, adventurer. I am sorry to have been so cryptic, but I could not risk alerting the mogu to my work here.

They are seeking something in the valley. Plundering the tombs of their old kings for relics of power.

I could not observe them long before having to flee, but I did manage to recover a relic of my own.

The Tongue of Ba-Shon will let us communicate securely over long distances, but only after I have bound it to myself.

I think I'm ready to begin, if you are.

passages.title: The Tongue of Ba-Shon
passages.text: I'll need to bind my essence to the Tongue, then you can use it to speak with me from anywhere.

passages.title: The Tongue of Ba-Shon
passages.text:
This must be a very powerful relic for Zuan to want it back so badly.

It frightens me to think of what else they may find in the tombs...

passages.title: Round 1: Brewmaster Chani
passages.text:
Welcome, Challenger, to my tournament of champions! Today we test the strengths of Pandaria's most dedicated heroes.

Your first opponent awaits you under the eastern gazebo. Defeat her, and you may proceed to the next round.

Fight with strength, fight with honor.

passages.title: Round 1: Brewmaster Chani
passages.text:
Without conflict, there can be no growth.

The need to change, to persevere, to improve, these are the traits that bring champions to my doorstep.

passages.title: Round 1: Brewmaster Chani
passages.text: Well done, challenger.

passages.title: Round 1: The Streetfighter
passages.text:
Welcome, challenger, to my tournament of champions! Today we test the strengths of Pandaria's most dedicated heroes.

Your first opponent awaits you under the eastern gazebo. Defeat her, and you may proceed to the next round.

Fight with strength, fight with honor.

passages.title: Round 1: The Streetfighter
passages.text:
Without conflict, there can be no growth.

The need to change, to persevere, to improve, these are the traits that bring champions to my doorstep.

passages.title: Round 1: The Streetfighter
passages.text: Well done, challenger.

passages.title: Round 2: Clever Ashyo & Ken-Ken
passages.text:
You may know your next challengers. They were arguing fiercely when they arrived, so I have charged them with fighting side by side.

This will teach them the strength of friendship, and possibly entertain me in the process.

Go to the north eastern arena and face this jinyu and hozen.

Do not be gentle, they need to learn to work together.

passages.title: Round 2: Clever Ashyo & Ken-Ken
passages.text: Strength can come from an ally as much as from one's self.

passages.title: Round 2: Clever Ashyo & Ken-Ken
passages.text:
Pity that those two did not learn their lesson yet. No matter. In time I am sure they will come to see wisdom.

In the meantime, congratulations on your victory.

passages.title: Round 2: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text:
Your next challenger is a Bramblestaff. Strength is in their blood. I remember a full century of only Bramblestaff champions.

No pressure, little <race>.

Go to the eastern arena north of here and face this young challenger. See first hand if strength is earned or inherited.

passages.title: Round 2: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text: I was once defeated in a match by a Bramblestaff. In my defense, he distracted me with a ball of yarn.

passages.title: Round 2: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text: Ah. The Bramblestaff family have long held the championship generation after generation. I am sure this one will take the title sooner or later as well.

passages.title: Round 3: The Wrestler
passages.text:
Your next challenger is a favorite of mine. He draws strength from raw force and determination.

Plus he has a mask.

Face him in the western arena when you are ready, and good luck.

passages.title: Round 3: The Wrestler
passages.text: Sometimes strength can come from the outside.

passages.title: Round 3: The Wrestler
passages.text: Well fought, challenger. That was a fierce opponent.

passages.title: Behind the Battlefront
passages.text:
This battlefront has been undermanned and unsupplied for too long during my absence in Kun-Lai. We need to get things back in order here before we can pick up the trail of the Sha of Hatred.

Taoshi is my best. I've sent her north to investigate rumors of mantid that have somehow made it through the battlefront. I need someone I can trust to get out there and work with her to plug any holes in our defenses.

If my reports on you are correct, I can trust you with this, right <class>?

passages.title: Behind the Battlefront
passages.text: You look capable. Taran knows to send me the best. I like that.

passages.title: Round 3: Master Boom Boom
passages.text:
Your next challenger found his strength on a beach. Particularly in a box labeled "dynamite."

He proves however that found strength can be as deadly as personal strength.

When you are ready, face this Master Boom Boom in the Western Arena.

passages.title: Round 3: Master Boom Boom
passages.text: Well fought, challenger. That was a fierce opponent.

passages.title: Unwelcome Intruders
passages.text:
Those are mantid scouts down there. Gao-Ran's Battlefront is meant to keep them out of eastern Townlong Steppes. If we allow them north of the barricade, we may lose our foothold here.

Let's clear them out. I'll be with you.

passages.title: Unwelcome Intruders
passages.text: This is where they're getting through, the eastern pass.

passages.title: Trap Setting
passages.text:
Good to meet you, <class>. We have traps all along the pass to help us catch mantid that might be sneaking through, but their numbers have been so great that most of the traps have already been triggered.

Taoshi said you might be able to reset some of them while you're out there. Can you help?

passages.title: Trap Setting
passages.text: These traps have been very effective, the mantid numbers are just getting out of hand in these past weeks.

passages.title: Trap Setting
passages.text: We could use a few more capable men like you around the camp. Thank you for your help, <class>.

passages.title: Back on Their Feet
passages.text:
<name>, I could use your help. With their long shifts, our warriors down at the southern front of the battlefront are fighting to the point of exhaustion, and many of them have been exposed to the mantid poison.

We need more people to tend to the wounded. I've prepared some bandages with the herbs you brought me, but if you have some healing skills, those might work even better.

Please, <name>, get our men back on their feet so that they can get back here to safety.

passages.title: Back on Their Feet
passages.text:
With the constant mantid attacks, the men are being worked to the bone. We are undermanned on all fronts.

Your help means a lot to us, <name>.

passages.title: Back on Their Feet
passages.text: There are several warriors that owe their lives to you. You have my deepest appreciation, <class>.

passages.title: The Endless Swarm
passages.text: Gao-ran's men need help down on the southern front. If you want to stand by the Shado-Pan, that's where you should do it.

passages.title: The Endless Swarm
passages.text: The men of the battlefront are growing to respect you. You clearly know how to fight.

passages.title: Thieves and Troublemakers
passages.text:
I can't catch the little buggers for the life of me.

Kill any you can get your hands on. And keep a close eye on your valuables, they like to steal anything that isn't tied down.

passages.title: Thieves and Troublemakers
passages.text: I haven't hated plants so much since my job back at Halfhill.

passages.title: Thieves and Troublemakers
passages.text:
I guess you're a bit faster than me. Well, thanks.

I'll try to finish collecting some orbs and get them back to camp while there's still some face to save.

passages.title: Cutting the Swarm
passages.text:
The mantid numbers have been increasing since you left for the cleft. Let's put these orbs you gathered to use.

Get down on the battlefront and man one of the cannons. Let none through.

passages.title: Cutting the Swarm
passages.text: I can't remember the last time they swarmed this thickly. They probably haven't within my lifetime.

passages.title: Cutting the Swarm
passages.text: We're not done yet...

passages.title: Terror of the Dread Wastes
passages.text:
That thing is huge!

The Shado-Pan holding the battlefront were never trained for something like this... let's get down there and take it out ourselves.

passages.title: Terror of the Dread Wastes
passages.text:
You. You're coming with me.

I've never seen someone handle themselves on the battlefield like that. I need a strong <class> like you with me when we face the Sha of Hatred.

passages.title: Along the Southern Front
passages.text:
I'm heading westward with Taoshi to gather the strongest I can find to confront the Sha of Hatred.

I would like you to come with me.

passages.title: Along the Southern Front
passages.text: Let's get this taken care of so we can get down to the bridge.

passages.title: Round 4: Master Windfur
passages.text:
Well done, challenger. You have reached the final round.

Your last opponent is a powerful master of the winds. He has defended his people for many years and stood as champion on more than one occasion.

Face this Master Windfur in the main arena when you are ready.

And challenger... good luck.

passages.title: Round 4: Master Windfur
passages.text: Congratulations, champion! The day is yours.

passages.title: Round 4: The P.U.G.
passages.text:
And now the final round. I have selected three challengers for you to face. This may seem unfair... to a weakling. You are not a weakling, correct?

Go to the main temple, stand in the grand arena, and face these three challengers. Prove you are stronger than their combined power!

Good luck, Challenger!

passages.title: Round 4: The P.U.G.
passages.text: Some find strength in numbers. I respect this idea, when it is properly executed.

passages.title: Round 4: The P.U.G.
passages.text:
Superb! What a battle!

You have proven yourself champion of this day's tournament. Well done!

You must return and put on such a show of strength in the future.

passages.title: Greenstone Village
Hui's Vengeance
A Trail of Fear
passages.text:
You now know Niuzao's secret. We are not only the wardens of this temple... we were the wardens of the Sha of Fear that was buried beneath it.

The Sha itself may have escaped... but it left traces behind. If you're truly going down into the catacombs, you should eliminate those traces, before they escape and cause greater problems than those we already face.

passages.title: A Trail of Fear
passages.text:
Even among our own order, only a few chosen elders knew of our sacred duty to contain the Sha of Fear.

Why they chose to tell the yak-keeper, I may never know.

passages.title: A Trail of Fear
passages.text: We already have mantid, mogu, and yaungol to worry about. This sha problem needs to be nipped in the bud before even we are overrun.

passages.title: Bad Yak
passages.text:
Is this the place where they replace defective yaks?

Can anybody help me out, here?

passages.title: Bad Yak
passages.text: This yak is not a good yak. Not at all.

passages.title: Bad Yak
passages.text: I think we made a pretty convincing argument. They'll HAVE to replace my yak now.

passages.title: Seeking Father
passages.text:
