It's time for Sully and I to leave. We'll keep our eyes out for any sign of the White Pawn and report back shortly.

I'm afraid I must leave you in charge while Admiral Taylor is recovering. Learn as much as you can from these jinyu while we are away. I expect a full report when we return.

passages.title: The Eye of the Naaru
passages.text:
The soulcore has transformed into a crystal. This is clearly the artifact that Kanrethad and Jubeka were attempting to create, but you still have no idea where they went.

Seek out the Black Prince in the Tavern of the Mists and see if you can acquire some information on where they went.

passages.title: Awaiting the Black Harvest
passages.text:
<name>, I have never heard of this Council of the Black Harvest. However, the fact that they are interested in my father's power concerns me greatly.

However, I do have... contacts, who may be able to help us track them down. Most of my agents are preoccupied with the Alliance and Horde battle in Krasarang. Once that has settled down, I will help you.

For now, feel free to leave the Naaru relic in my protection, or not - just don't end up dead somewhere at the bottom of a swamp. 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32360))

 if (cta) {
 $('.db-page-collection-tracker-cta').append(cta);
 }

passages.title: Tracking Event: Event Complete
passages.text:
It's time for Sully and I to leave. We'll keep our eyes out for any sign of the White Pawn and report back shortly.

I'm afraid I must leave you in charge while Admiral Taylor is recovering. Learn as much as you can from these jinyu while we are away. I expect a full report when we return.

passages.title: Pandaren Medicine
passages.text:
While I was in the Vale, I came across an ancient pandaren recipe for Memory Wine. I believe this brew can coax some helpful information out of Shan Kien.

I am needed here, so I have no choice but to ask you to find the ingredients for me.

The recipe can be found in a book near my other things, just behind me.

passages.title: A Lick of Fire
passages.text:
6 Ruqin Firewine. This intense liquor helps relax the mind, allowing the recovery of past memories.

<Scrawled along the side is another note.>

(Note: May result in a terrible hangover.)

passages.title: A Bit of Yak
passages.text:
3 Fresh Yak's Milk. Helps strengthen teeth and bones. Allows imbibers to return from their dream state.

<The now-familiar handwriting now leaves a cryptic message.>

(Why do all yaks look alike!?)

passages.title: The Measure of a Leader
passages.text:
We've progressed to a new part of the Pandaren campaign. The Alliance has landed on the shores with the full might of its navy. Your King aims to check Horde aggression in this new land.

Garrosh Hellscream is propelling the Horde headfirst into battle, but King Varian Wrynn is a little more of a mystery to me. Do you have a moment? I'd like to talk to you about this leader of yours.

passages.title: The Measure of a Leader
passages.text:
I am curious to see how King Wrynn rises to the occasion.

I am even more curious to see what YOU are capable of. Let's find out...

passages.title: A Dash of That
passages.text:
100 Buttonbelly Mushrooms. Must be freshly harvested from a wet, dark place.

<Scrawled along the edge of the page is a hand-written note.>

Fungus is very good for the health! (Or it might kill you, cause serious illness, rash, hallucination, or loosen bowels. Note to self - MUST be careful when selecting wild mushrooms!)

passages.title: Clearing a Path
passages.text:
First thing's first. If we're going to take the leader captive, we'll need to thin the numbers of his agents.

Be careful. These mogu are particularly dangerous - they appear to be manipulating the sha in ways we haven't seen before.

passages.title: Clearing a Path
passages.text: Good. We should be ready to make our move.

passages.title: Call of the Packmaster
passages.text:
<class>, through your eyes I've been able to witness the fighting along the coast, and the epic course of battles around the world. You've been very patient... and most informative.

I've also been keeping a close eye on your King. Would you be interested to hear what I've learned?

passages.title: Call of the Packmaster
passages.text: <A strange device sits within an ornate silk-lined chest. It appears as though it can be fastened to your sha-touched weapon as an additional upgrade. The empty socket is disconcerting; you feel as though it is staring back at you. A single, hollow, judgmental eye...>

passages.title: The Divine Bell
passages.text:
If the Alliance thought they could steal the Divine Bell from us, they were wrong!

Even now, we have them trapped in the crypts beneath us.

Death will be the price they pay for defying us.

Come, <class>. Let us show them the error of their ways.

passages.title: The Divine Bell
passages.text:
Darnassus, is it?

The Alliance believes they have won the day. Now, when their arrogance is at its greatest, is our opportunity to pluck the prize from their fingers.

passages.title: Breath of Darkest Shadow
passages.text:
Garrosh is right over there, and he's going to ring that bell at any moment.

We don't have time to wait for my father's army. This is our only chance to stop him!

I'll attempt to appeal to his senses before resorting to using the Harmonic Mallet.

Charge in whenever you're ready, <name>. I'll be right behind you.

passages.title: Breath of Darkest Shadow
passages.text:
<Anduin looks like a crumpled doll. He lays as still as a stone, and the only movement comes from the frigid air ruffling his fair, golden hair.>

<You sit quietly for a while, until the cold settles into your bones. The bell is destroyed, but the silence is deafening.>

<Out of the corner of your eye, you see the slightest flicker from the boy's hand. You lean in close. He breathes - but just barely! Anduin is alive!>

passages.title: The Situation In Dalaran
passages.text:
The night elves learned that the Divine Bell was stolen. This much we anticipated.

However, they've also found out that the "neutral" Sunreavers of Dalaran were complicit. Now, we've got a situation.

I need you to go to Dalaran. Speak with Kromthar for a ride. You are to rendezvous with Grand Magister Rommath once you arrive.

passages.title: The Situation In Dalaran
passages.text:
Good... you've arrived. It's not a good day to be Horde in Dalaran.

Jaina's called for the exile of all the Sunreavers. You and I are going to save as many as we can - including Archmage Aethas Sunreaver himself - and then get out of here as fast as possible.

passages.title: It Starts in the Sewers
passages.text:
Compared to the rest of the city, this part of the sewers is relatively calm. This is good - we can extract more Sunreavers in peace than we can in war.

Find as many citizens as you can. Tell them that it is not safe here, that they must leave the city at once.

And try to stay clear of the Silver Covenant. We don't want to cause a scene if we can avoid it. Not yet, anyhow.

passages.title: It Starts in the Sewers
passages.text: I think I see a few more Sunreavers over there...

passages.title: It Starts in the Sewers
passages.text: Let's press on.

passages.title: Hand of the Silver Covenant
passages.text:
Every Sunreaver Jaina expels from this city is a new blade that fights for the Horde. For US.

I'm off to gather more strong elves. You've proven your hand in combat thus far - go take care of that creep in the black market.

When you're done, we'll meet at the ramp and prepare to go aboveground.

passages.title: Hand of the Silver Covenant
passages.text:
The first stage of our mission is complete. That was the easy part.

<Rommath takes a deep, measured breath, then continues...>

passages.title: The Silver Covenant's Stronghold
passages.text:
I have it on good authority that Archmage Aethas Sunreaver is being held in the Silver Enclave, home of the Silver Covenant. Arcanist Rathaella holds him in captivity.

Most Covenant agents are out slaughtering Sunreavers right now, which means our chance is ripe. Slay Rathaella, and spring Aethas from his prison.

passages.title: The Silver Covenant's Stronghold
passages.text: We will continue saving Sunreavers for a while longer. Aethas' location may become clearer as we press on.

passages.title: Krasus' Landing
passages.text:
We can rescue as many Sunreavers as we want, but if they can't escape, then there's no point.

The Silver Covenant will certainly be subduing and killing the Sunreavers' dragonhawks. Put a stop to it.

passages.title: Krasus' Landing
passages.text: The depravity of this Silver Covenant sickens me. Attacking innocent creatures!

passages.title: Krasus' Landing
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Well done.

passages.title: A Return to Krasarang
passages.text:
Wherever your loyalties might lie - with Rommath and I, with Garrosh, or elsewhere - one thing is true: your acts today were truly heroic.

I can arrange for your transport back to Krasarang Wilds. Speak with me if you would like passage back to Pandaria, <name>.

passages.title: A Return to Krasarang
passages.text:
<Nazgrim listens as you recount the day's events.>

We take the bell... and the Alliance takes Dalaran. That escalated quickly.

War is coming, <name>. Be on your toes.

passages.title: Sewer Cleaning
passages.text:
Jaina's doing a good job taking care of Sunreavers above ground, but there's still plenty rooting around in the sewers.

Go find those lying rats and exterminate them!

passages.title: Sewer Cleaning
passages.text: <Vereesa looks out over her city.>

passages.title: Sewer Cleaning
passages.text: It's nice to have those rats out of here for good. Well done, hero.

passages.title: Cashing Out
passages.text:
I just saw one of the Sunreavers - Brasael, I think his name was - running off in the direction of the bank to the north. No doubt he's trying to gather whatever assets he can before he leaves.

Head him off and make sure he doesn't steal any resources from our coffers. He relinquished whatever funds he left in the bank when he and his Sunreaver kind betrayed us.

passages.title: Cashing Out
passages.text:
I suppose it wasn't enough for him to be a coward and a backstabber... he had to be a greedy thief as well.

Hmph. The Horde and the Sunreavers aren't all that different. They deserve one another.

passages.title: The Measure of a Leader
passages.text:
We've progressed to a new part of the Pandaren campaign. Your Warchief aims to impress the Pandaren with the full might of the Horde's military. He will lay claim to the resources of this land, with or without Pandaren aid.

I understand your leader's aims, but I really want to understand the Warchief himself. What drives him? And where is the Horde ultimately going? I'd like to talk to you about this leader of yours.

passages.title: The Measure of a Leader
passages.text:
Like all great leaders, Garrosh has greatly extended himself. Just what is he ultimately capable of?

More importantly, what YOU are capable of? Fresh bloodshed along the coast gives us an opportunity to find out...

passages.title: The Soul of the Horde
passages.text:
<class>, through your eyes I've been able to witness the fighting along the coast, and the epic course of battles around the world. You've been very patient... and most informative.

I've also been keeping a close eye on Garrosh Hellscream. Would you be interested to hear what I've learned?

passages.title: The Soul of the Horde
passages.text: <A strange device sits within an ornate silk-lined chest. It appears as though it can be fastened to your sha-touched weapon as an additional upgrade. The empty socket is disconcerting; you feel as though it is staring back at you. A single, hollow, judgmental eye...>

passages.title: Undermining the Under Miner
passages.text:
Grezik Oregrind has become a nuisance that must be eliminated.

This land responds to all of our actions as I am sure you are aware, <class>. Because of this, we cannot allow the goblins to haphazardly destroy it.

Our scouts have reported Sha emerging from Oregrind's Dig. The brains behind the operation is a goblin named Grezik Oregrind.

Destroy him and perhaps we will stall the operation just long enough to contain the Sha.

passages.title: Burning Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: You're back! Up for another battle with me?

passages.title: Burning Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: Think you can take me?

passages.title: Burning Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: I will get you next time!

passages.title: Flowing Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: You're back! Up for another battle with me?

passages.title: Flowing Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: Think you can take me?

passages.title: Flowing Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: I will get you next time!

passages.title: Whispering Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: You're back! Up for another battle with me?

passages.title: Whispering Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: Think you can take me?

passages.title: Whispering Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: I will get you next time!

passages.title: Thundering Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: You're back! Up for another battle with me?

passages.title: Thundering Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: Think you can take me?

passages.title: Thundering Pandaren Spirit
passages.text: I will get you next time!

passages.title: Impending Danger
passages.text:
Our scouts have sighted a fel command ship looming on the horizon, Grandmaster. It appears to be headed on a collision course with the Wandering Isle.

We should prepare our troops for the worst case situation - an all out attack.

In the meantime, let us send our champions ahead to try and divert the Legion ship's attention.

passages.title: Impending Danger
passages.text: The command ship appears to be gunning straight for us. We need everyone on alert, now!

passages.title: Impending Danger
passages.text: Our champions defeated the first wave of attackers, but the command ship is nearly upon us!

passages.title: Ties with the Past
passages.text:
While I was in the Vale, I came across an ancient pandaren recipe for Memory Wine. I believe this brew can coax some helpful information out of Shan Kien.

I am needed here, so I have no choice but to ask you to recover the essential ingredient for me. We need the spirit essence of a mogu that lived in the time of the memory we wish to see.

You should be able to find just such a spirit inside the Path of Conquerors, to the northeast.

passages.title: Ties with the Past
passages.text:
You never know what you will find in a book. Especially an ancient pandaren one.

I'm eager to see how this Memory Wine works.

passages.title: Ties with the Past
passages.text: Ah, very good. This is the last thing we needed.

passages.title: The Ruins of Ogudei
passages.text:
Our scouts at Sparkrocket Outpost have reported some new activity near an area called the Ruins of Ogudei.

We need to gather intelligence on what it is the Alliance are doing, and more importantly what it is they found. We cannot afford to have any unknowns.

Meet up with Belloc Brightblade in Sparkrocket Outpost and find out what he knows.

passages.title: The Ruins of Ogudei
passages.text: We have a lot of work to do, <class>. Who knows what has already been uncovered in Ogudei!

passages.title: The Time Is Now!
passages.text:
Now we take the fight to them, <class>!

Report to Shademaster Kiryn in Sparkrocket Outpost. She will have your orders.

Now we'll see how they handle the full might of the Horde rushing at their precious keep!

passages.title: The Time Is Now!
passages.text: Now things can get interesting! I have a few plans for Lion's Landing...

passages.title: Send A Message
passages.text:
It's time we show these Horde mongrels the full strength of the Alliance! Today we bring the battle to their door.

Report to Admiral Rogers aboard the Skyfire. She will have further instructions.

Good luck out there, <class>. Do the Alliance proud!

passages.title: Send A Message
passages.text: The battle is already underway, <class>. Let's get you out there!

passages.title: And Then There Were Goblins
passages.text:
We're fighting a war on all fronts, <class>. Even Pandaria itself needs our protection.

The Bilgewater goblins are destroying land that doesn't belong to them. They must be stopped!

Report to Sky Admiral Rogers aboard the Skyfire. From her vantage point she should have a good idea of where their weak spots are.

passages.title: And Then There Were Goblins
passages.text: It's about time we dealt with this nuisance. Those Bilgewater runts need to be taught a lesson!

passages.title: With the Wind's Blessing...
passages.text:
<An urgent plea reaches your ears.>

<name>! My father's fleet is making its way to Pandaria. With favorable winds, they could arrive any moment.

The Pandaren have a blessing that will give us good luck with the weather and speed our ships to these shores. We just need to collect charms of good fortune to make it happen.

As our ships draw closer to the island, less charms will be required. But if you have enough, we can speed them here right away...

<An urgent plea reaches your ears.>

<name>! The Horde fleet is making its way to Pandaria. With favorable winds, they could arrive any moment.

The Pandaren have a blessing that will give us good luck with the weather and speed our brothers and sisters to these shores. We simply need to collect charms of good fortune to gain fortune's favor.

As our ships draw closer to the island, less charms will be required. But if you have enough, we can speed them here right away...

passages.title: The Order of the Cloud Serpent
passages.text:
Ahhh, it seems you have found yourself the proud owner of a majestic cloud serpent.

Before you may fly the skies on this powerful creature, you must first earn the skill to ride it.

The Order of the Cloud Serpent can teach you the knowledge that you seek.

If you wish to follow our way, you should speak to Instructor Skythorn at The Arboretum in the Jade Forest.

I wish you luck, <race>.

passages.title: The Order of the Cloud Serpent
passages.text: Ah, have you come to join the Order?

passages.title: Sacrificial Prevention [PH]
passages.text:
The Zandalari Priests in the town to the north prepare the bodies of our fallen allies for sacrifice.

The best way to prevent this from happening? Kill them. Kill them all.

passages.title: Frighten Pterodactyls [PH]
passages.text:
The Pterodactyl Hatchlings being trained by Zandalari to the north are not yet the violent and savage beasts they are to become.

I believe we should save these creatures before the trolls corrupt them. If you could just frighten them off, perhaps some of them will be spared an unfortunate fate.

passages.title: The Creeping Carpet of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
Ah, roaches! I once bought a pet roach in the Undercity.

Roaches will soak up disease like a sponge, and then spread it as far as they can run. Which is pretty far.

Ihgaluk Crag is crawling with the things, and they carry Skumblade filth all over of this island. Crush as many of them as you can while you're there.

passages.title: The Creeping Carpet of Ihgaluk
passages.text: This should be fairly simple. Just smush them.

passages.title: The Creeping Carpet of Ihgaluk
passages.text: Every little bit helps.

passages.title: Left To Rot
passages.text:
The Skumblade saurok do not eat all of the meat they hunt. They reserve large portions of it to rot in piles near their homes, attracting pests and spreading disease.

We can't have the saurok spreading their disease beyond the borders of Ihgaluk Crag. Dispose of any excess meat that you find.

passages.title: Left To Rot
passages.text:
Left standing, those piles of discarded food are the perfect breeding ground for disease.

Were I still in the disease-spreading business, I'd consider using them myself.

passages.title: The Bloodletter
passages.text:
I have heard a disturbing report, <class>.

Just beyond our position, in the Court of Bone, the mogu bring captives to a general named Kaida the Bloodletter.

I will spare you the details, but he thrives on torturing his victims.

This monster must be stopped. If you fall to his blade, I wish you a swift death.

passages.title: The Bloodletter
passages.text: The mogu are capable of unimaginable cruelty.

passages.title: The Bloodletter
passages.text: I am glad to hear that this piece of filth is slain. You have done us all a great favor, <name>.

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text:
The Midsummer Fire Festival is a time to honor the elements. The element of fire stirs passion within us all. Many times, that passion pours out into aggressive actions. But here, in this land, we focus our passion on reverence.

We will honor the flame as tradition dictates. Will you honor the flame with us, <name>?

passages.title: Honor the Flame
passages.text: Honor the Dread Wastes flame.

We will honor the flame as tradition dictates. Will you honor the flame with us, <name>?

passages.title: Mission: The Secrets of Stormwind
A Wing to Fly On
passages.text:
I've just received a report that another young pterrorwing has been spotted in the Diremoor.

We need to recover as many of these as we can find. They may be the key to flying on this island.

passages.title: A Wing to Fly On
passages.text: A great gloom looms over this island...

passages.title: A Wing to Fly On
passages.text: Wonderful! I'll pass him off to our caretaker. Thank you.

passages.title: Skin of the Saurok
The Bloodletter
passages.text:
I have heard a disturbing report, <class>.

To the south, in the Court of Bones, the mogu bring captives to a general named Kaida the Bloodletter.

I will spare you the details, but he thrives on torturing his victims.

This monster must be stopped. If you fall to his blade, I wish you a swift death.

passages.title: Competing Magic
passages.text: My scouts have spotted a dangerous Zandalari just this side of Za'Tual. I need someone capable to see him dispatched. Are you up to the task?

passages.title: Competing Magic
passages.text: Your skills are impressive indeed. Thank you for doing this for me, <name>.

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text: My scouts have spotted a Zandalari war party on the northern beach. I need someone capable to see him dispatched. Are you up to the task?

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text: You have our gratitude, <name>.

passages.title: Imposing Threat
passages.text:
My scouts have spotted a mogu leader under the central tower. He needs to be killed before he can mount an offensive on our position.

Can you take care of this for me?

passages.title: Imposing Threat
passages.text: One less threat at our doorstep. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Beast Pens
passages.text:
We need to counter the beasts the Zandalari are using to strike at our camp. I have dispatched Scout Captain Elsia to the Beast Pens along with some war mages to provide cover.

Go and find her east of here near the breaches in the wall and help her trim down the cavalry and siege beasts being levied against us.

They are masked, so look for the shimmers of their magical cloaking spells.

passages.title: The Beast Pens
passages.text: I'm glad you were the one Lor'themar sent. These beasts are more than we can handle on our own. Time to spook the livestock.

passages.title: The Beating of Troll Drums
passages.text:
Do you hear that, <class>? The beating of war drums in the distance. The Zandalari are preparing for us.

Let's not give them the luxury of time to organize their defenses. We need to push the attack now!

Report to Scout Captain Elsia within Conqueror's Terrace. She will have further orders for you.

passages.title: The Beating of Troll Drums
passages.text:
These Zandalari are even more dangerous than we anticipated.

Do not make the mistake of underestimating them, for that may be the last mistake you make.

passages.title: Ashes of the Enemy
passages.text:
The mogu at the Court of Bones are bolstering their army by resurrecting the spirits of their dead.

We cannot allow them to revive their fallen warriors.

Take this torch and burn any mummified corpses that you can find.

We will destroy our enemies before they have a chance to rise.

passages.title: Ashes of the Enemy
passages.text: Their dead shall rise no more, thanks to you, <name>. Excellent work.

passages.title: The Call of Thunder
passages.text:
Within the graveyard, in the deepest ruins of their western crypt, the Thunder King's most powerful sorcerers are charging a lightning rod with crackling electricity.

We suspect that this weapon is meant to rain destruction on our stronghold at Violet Rise.

There is no time to delay. You must stop their ritual at once.

passages.title: The Call of Thunder
passages.text: Do not allow them to unleash the force of their weapon.

passages.title: The Call of Thunder
passages.text: You continue to exceed my expectations, <class>. Well done.

passages.title: The Bloodletter
passages.text:
I have heard a disturbing report, <class>.

Just beyond our position, in the Court of Bones, the mogu bring captives to a general named Kaida the Bloodletter.

He thrives on torturing his victims.

This monster must be stopped. If you fall to his blade, I wish you a swift death.

passages.title: The Bloodletter
passages.text: The mogu are capable of unimaginable cruelty.

passages.title: The Bloodletter
passages.text: I am glad to hear that this piece of filth is slain. You have done us all a great favor, <name>.

passages.title: Rise No More!
passages.text:
Have you seen the ghosts wandering the graveyard?

They are risen ancestors, the spirits of slain mogu who have been called back to this world.

When angered, they attack swiftly and silently, and their numbers increase by the day.

They do not belong here. Destroy them, and send them back beyond the grave.

passages.title: Rise No More!
passages.text: Wonderful work, <class>. This will help our offensive a great deal.

passages.title: Stone Cold
passages.text:
Our assault on the Court of Bones continues. Our progress remains slow, but measurable.

Unfortunately, we've received several reports of stone quilen statues coming to life without warning. These quilen are too dangerous to ignore.

Venture into the Court of Bones and destroy any quilen statues that you can find.

passages.title: Stone Cold
passages.text: I am glad to hear that you left the quilen in a thousand tiny pieces. They are little more than a nuisance to my work here on the island.

passages.title: The Skumblade Threat
passages.text:
Ihgaluk Crag has no end of saurok. Those beasts attack my men and spread their disease into nearby water and wildlife, interfering with our operations.

Thin their numbers, <name>. Once the Horde takes full control of this island, we can look for more permanent solutions.

passages.title: The Skumblade Threat
passages.text:
Ihgaluk Crag has no end of saurok. Those beasts attack my men and spread their disease into nearby water and wildlife, interfering with our operations.

Thin their numbers, <name>. Once the Alliance takes full control of this island, we can look for more permanent solutions.

passages.title: The Skumblade Threat
passages.text:
One day, this island will belong to the Alliance. I can only hope that it will be free of saurok before then.

<Modera sneers.>

At least they attack the Horde, too.

passages.title: Heinous Sacrifice
passages.text:
Some of the strongest of the spiritbinders perform heinous rites to their wretched gods.

We've devised a method to destroy their altars, so the difficult task will be getting to each altar alive.

Venture into the depths of Za'Tual and destroy their altars.

passages.title: Heinous Sacrifice
passages.text: I realize what I ask you to do is dangerous, but it is necessary.

passages.title: Heinous Sacrifice
passages.text: <class>, the destruction of those altars will force the trolls to halt their most heinous of sacrifices. You have the thanks of everyone here.

passages.title: Dark Offerings
passages.text:
The Zandalari's spiritbinders perform dark sacrifices to appease their gods, killing our people in the process.

Destroy any Zandalari offerings you can find in Za'Tual to help slow the pace of their dark sacrifices.

passages.title: Dark Offerings
passages.text: Without the offerings, they will need to collect more before their sacrifices can proceed. Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Harbingers of the Loa
passages.text:
If you spend some time in Za'Tual, you will likely see one of their large tents emanating a pure form of evil.

Please, venture into the troll camp and put a stop to these unspeakable rituals.

passages.title: Harbingers of the Loa
passages.text: Most who witness such rituals never return, and those that do tend to be shaken. You, <name>, seem little moved by your incredible deeds. I am impressed.

passages.title: Dangers of Za'Tual
passages.text:
The Zandalari are a formidable foe - more so than many foes we've encountered in the past. But you are a formidable foe as well, <name>.

Enter Za'Tual to and show them the risks associated with opposing the likes of you.

passages.title: Dangers of Za'Tual
passages.text: <name>, your help against the Zandalari is appreciated. I realize it seems we cannot stem the tide, but your efforts make a difference.

passages.title: Pterrible Ptorment
passages.text:
One of the trolls' skyscreamers in Za'Tual is undergoing a ritual of torture, its will being bent forever to serve its masters.

Kill those that inflict such torment on the creature and we can only hope that it will return to the skies.

passages.title: Pterrible Ptorment
passages.text: Have you freed the creature?

passages.title: Pterrible Ptorment
passages.text: I hope that creature has the intelligence necessary to know who saved it. It seems to me that it would be a dangerous foe if provoked.

passages.title: The Creeping Carpet of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
Ah, roaches! I once bought a pet roach in Booty Bay.

Roaches will soak up disease like a sponge, and then spread it as far as they can run. Which is pretty far.

Ihgaluk Crag is crawling with the things, and they carry Skumblade filth all over of this island. Crush as many of them as you can while you're there.

passages.title: The Creeping Carpet of Ihgaluk
passages.text: Every little bit helps.

passages.title: Left To Rot
passages.text:
The Skumblade saurok do not eat all of the meat they hunt. They reserve large portions of it to rot in piles near their homes, attracting pests and spreading disease.

We can't have the saurok spreading their disease beyond the borders of Ihgaluk Crag. Dispose of any excess meat that you find.

passages.title: Left To Rot
passages.text: I know of many ways to spread disease, but this one is novel.

passages.title: Left To Rot
passages.text:
Left standing, those piles of discarded food are the perfect breeding ground for disease.

Were I still in the disease-spreading business, I'd consider using them myself.

passages.title: Skin of the Saurok
passages.text:
Ihgaluk Crag is a dangerous place. Luckily, you have the magic of the Kirin Tor behind you.

I can transform you into a saurok.

I will perform the first half of the illusion on you now. Afterwards, you should go directly to Ihgaluk Crag and slay one of the Skumblade saurok. Once you have done this, I will contact you and complete the second half of the illusion. 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32549))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32549))");

passages.title: Saur Loser
passages.text:
Inside the Beast Pens you will encounter some of the most skilled beast tamers in the Zandalari military. They are trained to kill with axe, beast, and claw. This is where they build their cavalry.

We need you to kill any Zandalari you find in the Beast Pens before they can get their mounted monstrosities out into the open battlefield.

passages.title: Saur Loser
passages.text: These trolls have been using dark magics to achieve their goals. No patience, no honor. You have done the world a good service in reducing their numbers today.

passages.title: Loa-saur
passages.text:
The Zandalari have found a way to bind loa to their beasts giving them impressive and lethal powers.

We need to put a stop to this.

Search the Beast Pens for a loa speaker and slay him. You should be able to find them by keeping a look out for their glowing beasts.

We must not allow these atrocities to continue.

passages.title: Loa-saur
passages.text: I always believed the loa to be a simple troll superstition. These Zandalari are full of surprises.

passages.title: Loa-saur
passages.text: Well done, champion. These beasts are strong enough. We don't need them infused with an angry spirit now do we?

passages.title: Competing Magic
passages.text:
One of my scryers has identified a Zandalari leader near the central tower. He needs to be removed.

Would you be willing to do this for me, <class>?

passages.title: Competing Magic
passages.text: You're dependable, <name>. I like that.

passages.title: Imposing Threat
passages.text:
One of my scouts has returned with word of a mogu leader under the central tower. He needs to be removed.

Would you be willing to do this for me, <class>?

passages.title: Imposing Threat
passages.text: I appreciate what you've done for us this day, <name>.

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text:
We've spotted a Zandalari war party down on the beach just outside these walls. We need to eliminate them before returning to camp.

Are you up for the task?

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. That's a worry off my mind.

passages.title: Zandalari on the Rise
passages.text:
We've spotted a Zandalari leader up the central stairs. We need to eliminate him before returning to camp.

Can you handle this one?

passages.title: Zandalari on the Rise
passages.text: Yet again you prove yourself. We would be fortunate if all amongst us could aspire to your talents.

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text:
We've spotted a Zandalari war party up the beach. We need to eliminate him before returning to camp.

Would you be willing to handle this one?

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text: Your skills are impressive. You have our gratitude.

passages.title: The Beast Pens
passages.text:
I do not want to see another Zandalari beast rider breach our defenses!

I have dispatched Scout Captain Daelin and some war mages to the Beast Pens northwest of here. Their mission is to infiltrate and harass the Zandalari siege and cavalry units. I want you to join them and lend your expertise.

Keep an eye out for the tell tale shimmer of their magical cloaking spell.

passages.title: The Beast Pens
passages.text: Today, we hunt the hunters!

passages.title: No Time To Rest
passages.text:
We have accomplished much since arriving here, but now is not the time to rest. Your efforts have helped us breach the upper level of the Thunder King's stronghold.

Now, I call on you to continue our campaign. Report to Scout Captain Daelin within Conqueror's Terrace. He will have further orders for you.

passages.title: No Time To Rest
passages.text:
The Zandalari here are not to be under-estimated, <class>. Powerful magic overwhelms this space.

We must be diligent in our efforts.

passages.title: Trailing Light in the Dark
passages.text:
There is some dark magic in the Diremoor that extinguishes even our magical illuminations, and so our scouts struggle to find their way.

As you pass through the swamp, relight any torches you find that our men might find their way. Perhaps they will help you find your way back as well.

passages.title: A Wing to Fly On
passages.text:
I've just received a report that another young pterrorwing has been spotted in the Diremoor.

We need to recover as many of these as we can find. They may be the key to flying on this island.

passages.title: A Wing to Fly On
passages.text: A great gloom looms over this island...

passages.title: A Wing to Fly On
passages.text: Wonderful! I'll pass him off to our caretaker. Thank you.

passages.title: The Sleepless Legion
passages.text: The Shan'ze are animating an army from the statues in the center of the isle, an army that batters our defenses day and night. Destroy any of the walking statues you see. Our defenders will greatly appreciate it.

passages.title: The Sleepless Legion
passages.text: You are not done just yet, <class>.

passages.title: The Sleepless Legion
passages.text: Your efforts are appreciated, <class>.

passages.title: Enemies Beneath the Tower
passages.text: There are mogu in the Diremoor animating the army of statues near the tower. Vereesa wants them dead. I think you're the one to do it.

passages.title: Enemies Beneath the Tower
passages.text: Well done, <class>. Thank you for the help.

passages.title: The Shuddering Moor
passages.text:
There is an immense beast in the swamp. It has not yet marched upon us, but I place no stock that we will continue to be so fortunate.

Strike it down before it grows hungry enough to brave our defenses.

passages.title: The Shuddering Moor
passages.text:
You are not one to be trifled with. I am sure to have further use of your services.

Come back to me in a day's time, <class>.

passages.title: The Zandalari Colossus
passages.text: The trolls have dispatched one of their immense constructs on the southern road, blocking our passage around the island. See to it that the road is cleared, <class>.

passages.title: The Zandalari Colossus
passages.text:
When I give you a task, it gets handled.

Well done, <class>.

passages.title: Competing Magic
passages.text:
One of the scryers has identified a Zandalari leader near the central tower. He needs to be removed.

Would you be willing to handle this?

passages.title: Competing Magic
passages.text: You're dependable, <name>. I like that.

passages.title: Imposing Threat
passages.text:
One of Vereesa's scouts has returned with word of a mogu leader under the central tower. He needs to be removed.

Would you be willing to handle this?

passages.title: Imposing Threat
passages.text: I appreciate what you've done for us this day, <name>.

passages.title: Among the Bones
passages.text: The scouts have spotted a dangerous Zandalari among the bones west of Ihgaluk Crag. We need someone capable to see him dispatched. Are you up to the task?

passages.title: Among the Bones
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: Among the Bones
passages.text: It's good to have a man I can trust close at hand.

passages.title: Competing Magic
passages.text: The scouts have spotted a dangerous Zandalari just this side of Za'Tual. We need someone capable to see him dispatched. Are you up to the task?

passages.title: Competing Magic
passages.text: Your skills are impressive indeed. Thank you for doing this for me, <name>.

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text:
We've received word of a Zandalari war party up the beach, north of our foothold. We need them hunted down and killed.

Are you willing to do this thing for us, <class>?

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text: You have our gratitude, <name>.

passages.title: Imposing Threat
passages.text:
The scryers have spotted a mogu leader at the central tower. He needs to be killed before he can mount an offensive on our position.

Can you take care of this for us?

passages.title: Imposing Threat
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: Imposing Threat
passages.text: One less threat at our doorstep. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Raining Bones
passages.text:
We've spotted a Zandalari leader up the central stairs. We need to eliminate him before returning to camp.

Would you be willing to do the deed?

passages.title: Raining Bones
passages.text: You're a good <class> to have around, that's for certain. Thank you.

passages.title: Zandalari on the Rise
passages.text:
We've spotted a Zandalari leader up the central stairs. We need to eliminate him before returning to camp.

Can you handle this one?

passages.title: Zandalari on the Rise
passages.text: Yet again you prove yourself. We would be fortunate if all amongst us could aspire to your talents.

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text:
We've spotted a Zandalari war party down on the beach just outside these walls. We need to eliminate them before returning to camp.

Are you up for the task?

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. That's a worry off my mind.

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text:
We've spotted a Zandalari war party up the beach. We need to eliminate him before returning to camp.

Would you be willing to handle this one?

passages.title: Encroaching Force
passages.text: Your skills are impressive. You have our gratitude.

passages.title: Secrets of the First Empire
passages.text:
For two thousand years the mogu ruled this entire land. So brutal was their regime that its name is never uttered aloud: Pandaren call it either the "Old Kingdom" or "First Dynasty."

The Thunder King was its founder and first emperor. He amassed enormous power on what is now the Isle of Thunder.

His time has passed, <name>. We should claim some of his power for ourselves. Gather mogu relics for me from the Throne of Thunder, and amass some trillium - I have a plan!

passages.title: Secrets of the First Empire
passages.text: What have you uncovered from the Throne of Thunder? Is the Thunder King's ferocious reputation warranted?

passages.title: Secrets of the First Empire
passages.text:
<Wrathion inspects the treasures you brought him.>

Well done. The trillium will need additional refinement, of course, but these samples are pure.

I will need to study these artifacts for a time but I believe I can use the knowledge contained here to craft something of great value to us both.

passages.title: The Zandalari Prophecy
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

I have read your reports on the Zandalari and believe I have some clues as to their most recent aggression.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: The Zandalari Prophecy
passages.text:
No wonder the Zandalari have come. They are in need of a new home, and I am sure their mogu allies have promised them much.

We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: Rumbles of Thunder
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

The foreboding sound of thunder has haunted my people for generations. And as you have discovered in your own research, Lei Shen is at the heart of that fear.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: Rumbles of Thunder
passages.text:
What we know of Lei Shen are dark legends that have been remembered over the vast span of time. I often wondered if these legends had exaggerated the power of Lei Shen. But your research would suggest they may have greatly underestimated the Thunder King. These are dark days indeed.

We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: Gods and Monsters
passages.text:
Dear adventurer,

Is it true that the mogu are really connected to the titans? I find this very hard to believe. But looking over your research, some of the truth about the mogu begins to take shape.

If you visit us at the Seat of Knowledge in Vale of Eternal Blossoms we can add this contribution to your personal collection.

Thank you for your diligence!

Sincerely,

Lorewalker Cho

passages.title: Gods and Monsters
passages.text:
Your research is most distressing. But it sheds light on a truth we have long sought: "Where did the mogu come from? And why were they such tyrants?"

We will add this knowledge to your collection. If you wish me to narrate this for you, simply point at the correct volume in your Private Collection.

passages.title: Beasts of Fable
passages.text: Have you ever read the great Pandaren book of fables? Pandaren pass these stories on to their cubs - stories of the cricket and the hawk, or the slow-moving turtle - to teach them lessons that they will find useful in life. What few cubs know is that these creatures exist, here, in Pandaria! Though the stories of their travels are made up, they are powerful denizens of this world. Should you happen upon them in your travels, you may test the might of your pets against their storied statures.

passages.title: Beasts of Fable
passages.text: You found them all? Amazing! So the stories ARE true! Perhaps you will write the next great Pandaren fable based on your own incredible journey!

passages.title: Beasts of Fable Book I
passages.text: The stories of Ka'wi the Gorger, Nitun, Kafi, and Dos-Ryga will exist in this land, always. Do you wish to meet them in battle once more?

passages.title: Beasts of Fable Book I
passages.text: Do you return victorious?

passages.title: Beasts of Fable Book I
passages.text: I bow to you who continues to walk in the footfalls of the great Pandaren fables.

passages.title: Giant Dinosaur Bone
passages.text: <Ku'ma shrugs.>

passages.title: More Giant Dinosaur Bones
passages.text: Bones bones bones bones bones...

passages.title: Many More Giant Dinosaur Bones
passages.text: Too many, not enough, no no...give them to Ku'ma...

passages.title: Learn To Ride
passages.text: It's time for you to learn how to ride! Seek out Randal Hunter at the Eastvale Logging Camp in Elwynn Forest. Don't forget to buy your mount while you are there!

passages.title: Learn To Ride
passages.text: Don't forget to buy your mount while you are here!  Katie Hunter can be found here in camp.

passages.title: Made for War
passages.text:
Some things are built with multiple purposes in mind. Some things are built with the sole purpose of destruction.

A massive construct called the Pyrestar Demolisher sits guarding Dawnseeker Promontory. Its purpose is solely to destroy. It must be dismantled.

passages.title: Made for War
passages.text:
Excellent work, <race>. The problem with constructs is they can always be rebuilt.

I imagine it will not take the Sunreavers long to build a new death machine.

passages.title: Mana Scavengers
passages.text:
Sometimes, even the smallest creatures can be the biggest threat.

The Sunreavers brought mana wyrms with them. Though small in size they have the ability to cripple our casters in combat. Many have learned the hard way not to underestimate them.

They must be dealt with and quickly.

passages.title: Mana Scavengers
passages.text: You've made excellent progress today, <class>. Rest assured however, our work here is nowhere close to done.

passages.title: Work Order: Dominance Offensive I
passages.text:
<Yoon's writing decorates the page though his feelings seem conflicted.>

I normally try to stay out of conflict, but an order is an order. Since you are of the Horde I decided to pass this order your way.

The Dominance Offensive has requested an order of red blossom leeks.

The troops down there just can't seem to get enough of them! 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32642))");

passages.title: Work Order: Operation: Shieldwall I
passages.text:
<Yoon's writing decorates the page though his feelings seem conflicted.>

I normally try to stay out of conflict, but an order is an order. Since you are of the Alliance I decided to pass this order your way.

Operation: Shieldwall has requested a whole heap of witchberries.

I can't be sure, but I think they have an idea to use them in some sort of weapon. 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32645))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32645))");

passages.title: Work Order: Golden Lotus I
passages.text:
<Yoon kept this order request short.>

The Golden Lotus have requested a large number of white turnips.

Their request mentioned something about trouble-making sprites wreaking havoc on Mistfall Village. Apparently the sprites don't like turnips! 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32647))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32647))");

passages.title: Work Order: Shado-Pan I
passages.text:
<Yoon's writing seems rushed. He must have been excited.>

The Shado-Pan want crops from you! What an honor indeed!

A request came in this morning for green cabbages. Apparently, they make a rather tasty cabbage soup with them.

Only the finest will do for the Shado-Pan! 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32649))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32649))");

passages.title: To the Skies!
passages.text:
We have a plan to halt the mogu's weaponmaking capabilities, and it involves the creature you recovered from the Zandalari.

Speak to me when you're ready to learn more.

passages.title: To the Skies!
passages.text: It's time to begin your mission!

passages.title: To the Skies!
passages.text: Incredible work. This presents us with a monumental opportunity.

passages.title: Work Order: The August Celestials I
passages.text:
<Yoon's familiar writing scrolls across the tattered paper.>

The trainees out at the Cradle of Chi-Ji are in need of striped melons. Apparently, they use them in their training exercises.

A representative will be by tomorrow to collect whatever striped melons you can spare. 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32653))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32653))");

passages.title: The Fall of Shan Bu
passages.text:
Lei Shen found a clutch of rare storm dragon eggs early in his campaign. One - known as Nalak - was particularly brutal and killed all of its handlers, so he took it for his own.

Now, Shan Bu, one of Lei Shen's most loyal servants, works to resurrect the dragon.

It is time for us to strike against Shan Bu!

Speak to me when you are ready to launch the assault!

passages.title: The Fall of Shan Bu
passages.text: The time to defeat Shan Bu is now!

passages.title: The Fall of Shan Bu
passages.text: You've done it, <class>! Shan Bu is dead once and for all, and we've learned that Lor'themar may not be all that he seems.

passages.title: Work Order: The Klaxxi I
passages.text:
<Though Yoon's writing leaves something to be desired, it's nice to still have a little piece of him on the farm.>

An order came in this morning from the Klaxxi. Strangely enough they are requesting mogu pumpkins for some kind of research.

I find it's best not to ask them too many questions...

Best get started on their order. I'd hate to see what a bug of that size could do to your crops if you don't! 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32658))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(32658))");

passages.title: I Believe You Can Fly
passages.text:
The skies call out to you! It's time to learn to fly!

Visit the flying trainer, Maztha, at the Skyway in Orgrimmar.

And don't forget to buy a flying mount!

passages.title: I Believe You Can Fly
passages.text:
Ah, good to see you. You look like you are ready to take to the skies!

Remember, you can buy a flying mount from Drakma, just behind me.

passages.title: I Believe You Can Fly
passages.text:
The skies call out to you! It's time to learn to fly!

Visit the flying trainer, Bralla Cloudwing, at the Gryphon Roost in Stormwind.

And don't forget to buy a flying mount!

passages.title: I Believe You Can Fly
passages.text:
Ah, good to see you. You look like you are ready to take to the skies!

Remember, you can buy a flying mount from Tannec Stonebeak over there.

passages.title: The Storm Gathers
passages.text:
There is no time to waste, <name>. Every moment we delay here gives the Sunreavers more of a hold on the Isle.

Lady Jaina Proudmoore awaits us. We should not make her wait any longer.

Speak to me when you are ready to depart. I will escort you there myself.

passages.title: The Storm Gathers
passages.text: The key to our safety lies here, <name>. I feel it to my core that we are meant to be here.

passages.title: The Storm Gathers
passages.text: You have arrived just in time, <name>. This land needs to be controlled by the Kirin Tor for everyone's safety. This will not be an easy task.

passages.title: Inherit the Earth
passages.text:
As you know, <name>, I'm getting along in my years. One can't stay a spry young pandaren forever, you know.

I'm looking for someone to take over my duties here at the Tillers Union, and I can't think of a better person than Farmer Yoon.

He's got a good deal to learn, but he's got a good head on his shoulders and most importantly, a generous heart.

Do you think he'd be interested?

passages.title: Inherit the Earth
passages.text: Why I just knew you could convince him, <name>. You've set my heart at ease, knowing the Tillers will be in good hands.

passages.title: You Want Fish?
passages.text: Are you looking for golden carp? or some other Pandaren fish? I'm no fisherman myself, but there is a fellow by the river who has been teaching the folks traveling through here. If you go speak with him, he will likely give you some fish, as well as teach you how to fish.

passages.title: You Want Fish?
passages.text: Ah!  Have you come to learn how to fish? You're talking to the right person. First, here - have some fish!

passages.title: Pristine Banner of the Mantid Empire
passages.text: This artifact has been restored to a remarkably excellent condition. Perhaps you will put it on display at the Seat of Knowledge, so that lorewalkers and archaeologists can study it.
